497: static int beken_wlan_sta_passwd(FAR struct netdev_lowerhalf_s *dev,
498:                              FAR struct iwreq *iwr, bool set)
499: {
500:   int ret;
501:   struct iw_encode_ext *ext = iwr->u.encoding.pointer;
502:   uint8_t *pdata;
503:   uint8_t len;
504: #ifdef CONFIG_DEBUG_WIRELESS_INFO
505:   char buf[WIFI_PASSWORD_LEN];
506: #endif
507: 
508:   DEBUGASSERT(ext != NULL);
509: 
510:   pdata = ext->key;
511:   len   = ext->key_len;
512:   if (set)
513:     {
514:       if (len > WIFI_PASSWORD_LEN)
515:         {
516:           return -EINVAL;
517:         }
518: 
519:       memset(g_sta_config.password, 0x0, WIFI_PASSWORD_LEN);
520:       memcpy(g_sta_config.password, pdata, len);
521:       if (g_sta_config.ssid[0] != '\0')
522:         {
523:           ret = bk_wifi_sta_set_config(&g_sta_config);
524:           if (ret)
525:             {
526:               wlerr("ERROR: Failed to set Wi-Fi config data ret=%d\n", ret);
527:               return wifi_errno_trans(ret);

529:         }
530:     }
531:   else
532:     {
533:       wifi_sta_config_t sta_config;
534:       memset(&sta_config, 0x0, sizeof(wifi_sta_config_t));
535:       ret = bk_wifi_sta_get_config(&sta_config);
536:       if (ret != BK_OK)
537:         {
538:           wlerr("ERROR: Failed to ger Wi-Fi config data ret=%d\n", ret);
539:           return wifi_errno_trans(ret);
540:         }
541:       ext->key_len = strlen(sta_config.password);
542:       memcpy(pdata, sta_config.password, ext->key_len);
543:       if (g_is_sta_connected)
544:         {
545:           wifi_link_status_t link_status;
546:           bk_err_t rtn;

548:           rtn = bk_wifi_sta_get_link_status(&link_status);

559:               case WIFI_SECURITY_WPA_TKIP:

562:                 break;
563:               case WIFI_SECURITY_WPA_AES:
564:               case WIFI_SECURITY_WPA2_AES:
565:                 ext->alg = IW_ENCODE_ALG_CCMP;
566:                 break;
567:               default:
568:                 break;
569:             }
570:           }
571:           else
572:             {
573:               wlerr("ERROR: Failed to get link status=%d\n", rtn);
574:             }
575:         }
576:     }
577: 
578: #ifdef CONFIG_DEBUG_WIRELESS_INFO
579:   memcpy(buf, pdata, len);
580:   buf[len] = 0;
581:   wlinfo("INFO: Wi-Fi station password=%s len=%d\n", buf, len);

584:   return OK;

845: /****************************************************************************
846: * Name: build_scan_results
847: *
848: * Description:
849: *   Format the scan data to respond to wapi command
850: *
851: * Input Parameters:
852: *   scan_req - The private structure to keep the data buffer
853: *   info     - The scan AP data
854: *
855: * Returned Value:
856: *   OK on success.Negated errno returned on failure.
857: *
858: ****************************************************************************/
859: 
860: static int build_scan_results(FAR struct iw_scan_result_s *scan_req,
861:                              wifi_scan_ap_info_t *info)
862: {
863:   int need_len;
864:   FAR char *pointer;
865:   FAR struct iw_event *iwe;
866: 
867: 
868:   need_len = IW_EV_LEN(ap_addr) + IW_EV_LEN(qual) +
869:              IW_EV_LEN(freq) + IW_EV_LEN(data) + IW_EV_LEN(essid);
870: 
871:   if (scan_req->cur_len + need_len > scan_req->total_len)
872:     {
873:       scan_req->cur_len += need_len;
874:       return -E2BIG;
875:     }
876: 
877:   /* Copy scan result */
878: 
879:   pointer = scan_req->buf + scan_req->cur_len;
880: 
881:   /* 1.Copy BSSID */
882: 
883:   iwe                      = (FAR struct iw_event *)pointer;
884:   iwe->cmd                 = SIOCGIWAP;
885:   iwe->u.ap_addr.sa_family = ARPHRD_ETHER;
886:   memcpy(&iwe->u.ap_addr.sa_data, info->bssid, IFHWADDRLEN);
887:   iwe->len                 = IW_EV_LEN(ap_addr);
888:   pointer                 += iwe->len;
889: 
890:   /* 2.Copy ESSID */
891: 
892:   iwe                  = (FAR struct iw_event *)pointer;
893:   iwe->cmd             = SIOCGIWESSID;
894:   iwe->u.essid.flags   = 0;
895:   iwe->u.essid.length  = MIN(strlen(info->ssid), 32);
896:   iwe->u.essid.pointer = (FAR void *)sizeof(iwe->u.essid);
897:   memcpy(&iwe->u.essid + 1, info->ssid, iwe->u.essid.length);
898:   iwe->len             = IW_EV_LEN(essid) + ((iwe->u.essid.length + 3) & ~3);
899:   pointer             += iwe->len;
900: 
901:   /* 3.Copy link quality info */
902: 
903:   iwe                  = (FAR struct iw_event *)pointer;
904:   iwe->cmd             = IWEVQUAL;
905:   iwe->u.qual.qual     = 0;
906:   iwe->u.qual.level    = info->rssi;
907:   iwe->u.qual.noise    = 0;
908:   iwe->u.qual.updated  = IW_QUAL_DBM;
909:   iwe->len             = IW_EV_LEN(qual);
910:   pointer             += iwe->len;
911: 
912:   /* 4.Copy AP control channel */
913: 
914:   iwe                  = (FAR struct iw_event *)pointer;
915:   iwe->cmd             = SIOCGIWFREQ;
916:   iwe->u.freq.e        = 0;
917:   iwe->u.freq.m        = info->channel;
918:   iwe->len             = IW_EV_LEN(freq);
919:   pointer             += iwe->len;
920: 
921:   /* 5.Copy AP encryption mode */
922: 
923:   iwe                  = (FAR struct iw_event *)pointer;
924:   iwe->cmd             = SIOCGIWENCODE;
925:   iwe->u.data.flags    = info->security != WIFI_SECURITY_NONE?
926:                          IW_ENCODE_ENABLED :
927:                          IW_ENCODE_DISABLED;
928:   iwe->u.data.length   = 0;
929:   iwe->u.essid.pointer = NULL;
930:   iwe->len             = IW_EV_LEN(data);
931:   pointer             += iwe->len;
932: 
933:   scan_req->cur_len    = pointer - scan_req->buf;
934:   return OK;
935: }

962: /****************************************************************************
963: * Name: beken_wlan_sta_scan
964: *
965: * Description:
966: *   Trigger Wi-Fi station scan action
967: *
968: * Input Parameters:
969: *   dev - Reference to the NuttX driver state structure
970: *   iwr - The argument of the ioctl cmd
971: *   set - true: set data; false: get data
972: 
973: * Returned Value:
974: *   OK on success.Negated errno returned on failure.
975: *
976: ****************************************************************************/
977: 
978: static int beken_wlan_sta_scan(FAR struct netdev_lowerhalf_s *dev,
979:                            FAR struct iwreq *iwr, bool set)
980: {
981:   int ret = OK;
982:   if (set)
983:     {
984:       struct iw_scan_req* req = (struct iw_scan_req*)iwr->u.data.pointer;
985:       bk_event_register_cb(EVENT_MOD_WIFI, EVENT_WIFI_SCAN_DONE, wlan_scan_done_cb, NULL);
986:       if (req->essid_len > 0)
987:         {
988:           wifi_scan_config_t scan_config;
989:           memset(&scan_config, 0x0, sizeof(wifi_scan_config_t));
990:           scan_config.scan_type = req->scan_type;
991:           strncpy(scan_config.ssid, (char *)req->essid, WIFI_SSID_STR_LEN);
992:           bk_wifi_scan_start(&scan_config);
993:         }
994:       else
995:         {
996:           bk_wifi_scan_start(NULL);
997:         }
998:         g_scan_done = false;
999:     }
1000:   else
1001:     {
1002:       wifi_scan_result_t scan_result = {0};
1003:       struct iw_scan_result_s scan_req;
1004:       if (g_scan_done == false)
1005:         {
1006:           return -EAGAIN;
1007:         }
1008:       else if (iwr->u.data.length == 0)
1009:         {
1010:           return -E2BIG;
1011:         }
1012:       bk_wifi_scan_get_result(&scan_result);
1013: 
1014:       scan_req.buf       = iwr->u.data.pointer;
1015:       scan_req.cur_len   = 0;
1016:       scan_req.total_len = iwr->u.data.length;
1017:       for (int i = 0; i < scan_result.ap_num; i++)
1018:         {
1019:           ret = build_scan_results(&scan_req, &scan_result.aps[i]);
1020:           if (OK != ret)
1021:             {
1022:               wlerr("build_scan_results faild\n");
1023:             }
1024:         }
1025:       iwr->u.data.length = scan_req.cur_len;
1026:       bk_wifi_scan_free_result(&scan_result);
1027:       g_scan_done = false;
1028:     }
1029: 
1030:   return ret;
1031: }

585: /****************************************************************************
586:  * Network device driver functions
587:  *
588:  * These functions are used by a network device driver for interacting
589:  * with the NuttX network.
590:  *
591:  * Process an incoming IP packet.
592:  *
593:  * This function should be called when the device driver has received
594:  * a packet from the network. The packet from the device driver must
595:  * be present in the d_buf buffer, and the length of the packet
596:  * should be placed in the d_len field.
597:  *
598:  * When the function returns, there may be an outbound packet placed
599:  * in the d_buf packet buffer. If so, the d_len field is set to
600:  * the length of the packet. If no packet is to be sent out, the
601:  * d_len field is set to 0.
602:  *
603:  * The usual way of calling the function is presented by the source
604:  * code below.
605:  *
606:  *     dev->d_len = devicedriver_poll();
607:  *     if (dev->d_len > 0)
608:  *       {
609:  *         ipv4_input(dev);
610:  *         if (dev->d_len > 0)
611:  *           {
612:  *             devicedriver_send();
613:  *           }
614:  *       }
615:  *
616:  * Note: If you are writing a network device driver that needs ARP
617:  * (Address Resolution Protocol), e.g., when running the network over
618:  * Ethernet, you will need to call the network ARP code before calling
619:  * this function:
620:  *
621:  *     dev->d_len = ethernet_devicedrver_poll();
622:  *     if (dev->d_len > 0)
623:  *       {
624:  *         if (ETHBUF->type == HTONS(ETHTYPE_IP))
625:  *           {
626:  *             arp_ipin();
627:  *             ipv4_input(dev);
628:  *             if (dev->d_len > 0)
629:  *               {
630:  *                 arp_out();
631:  *                 devicedriver_send();
632:  *               }
633:  *           }
634:  *         else if (ETHBUF->type == HTONS(ETHTYPE_ARP))
635:  *           {
636:  *             arp_input();
637:  *             if (dev->d_len > 0)
638:  *               {
639:  *                 devicedriver_send();
640:  *               }
641:  *           }
642:  *
643:  ****************************************************************************/
644: 
645: #ifdef CONFIG_NET_IPv4
646: int ipv4_input(FAR struct net_driver_s *dev);
647: #endif
648: 
649: #ifdef CONFIG_NET_IPv6
650: int ipv6_input(FAR struct net_driver_s *dev);
651: #endif

653: #ifdef CONFIG_NET_6LOWPAN
654: struct radio_driver_s;   /* Forward reference.  See radiodev.h */
655: struct iob_s;            /* Forward reference See iob.h */

657: int sixlowpan_input(FAR struct radio_driver_s *ieee,
658:                     FAR struct iob_s *framelist, FAR const void *metadata);

663: /****************************************************************************
664:  * Name: arp_input
665:  *
666:  * Description:
667:  *   This function should be called by the Ethernet device driver when an ARP
668:  *   packet has been received.   The function will act differently
669:  *   depending on the ARP packet type: if it is a reply for a request
670:  *   that we previously sent out, the ARP cache will be filled in with
671:  *   the values from the ARP reply.  If the incoming ARP packet is an ARP
672:  *   request for our IP address, an ARP reply packet is created and put
673:  *   into the d_buf buffer.
674:  *
675:  *   On entry, this function expects that an ARP packet with a prepended
676:  *   Ethernet header is present in the d_buf buffer and that the length of
677:  *   the packet is set in the d_len field.
678:  *
679:  *   When the function returns, the value of the field d_len indicates
680:  *   whether the device driver should send out the ARP reply packet or not.
681:  *   If d_len is zero, no packet should be sent; If d_len is non-zero, it
682:  *   contains the length of the outbound packet that is present in the d_buf
683:  *   buffer.
684:  *
685:  ****************************************************************************/
686: 
687: void arp_input(FAR struct net_driver_s *dev);

689: #else /* CONFIG_NET_ARP */

697: /****************************************************************************
698:  * Polling of connections
699:  *
700:  * These functions will traverse each active network connection structure
701:  * and perform appropriate operations:  devif_poll() will perform TCP
702:  * and UDP polling operations. devif_poll() may be called asynchronously
703:  * from the network driver can accept another outgoing packet.
704:  *
705:  * In both cases, these functions will call the provided callback function
706:  * for every active connection. Polling will continue until all connections
707:  * have been polled or until the user-supplied function returns a non-zero
708:  * value (which it should do only if it cannot accept further write data).
709:  *
710:  * When the callback function is called, there may be an outbound packet
711:  * waiting for service in the device packet buffer, and if so the d_len field
712:  * is set to a value larger than zero. The device driver should then send
713:  * out the packet.
714:  *
715:  * Example:
716:  *   int driver_callback(FAR struct net_driver_s *dev)
717:  *   {
718:  *     if (dev->d_len > 0)
719:  *       {
720:  *         devicedriver_send();
721:  *         return 1; <-- Terminates polling if necessary
722:  *       }
723:  *     return 0;
724:  *   }
725:  *
726:  *   ...
727:  *   devif_poll(dev, driver_callback);
728:  *
729:  * Note: If you are writing a network device driver that needs ARP (Address
730:  * Resolution Protocol), e.g., when running the networ over Ethernet, you
731:  * will need to call the arp_out() function in the callback function
732:  * before sending the packet:
733:  *
734:  *   int driver_callback(FAR struct net_driver_s *dev)
735:  *   {
736:  *     if (dev->d_len > 0)
737:  *       {
738:  *         arp_out();
739:  *         devicedriver_send();
740:  *         return 1; <-- Terminates polling if necessary
741:  *       }
742:  *
743:  *     return 0;
744:  *   }
745:  *
746:  *   Compatible with all old flat buffer NICs
747:  *
748:  *                 tcp_poll()/udp_poll()/pkt_poll()/...(l3/l4)
749:  *                            /              \
750:  *                           /                \
751:  * devif_poll_[l3/l4]_connections()     devif_iob_send() (nocopy:udp/icmp/..)
752:  *            /                                   \      (copy:tcp)
753:  *           /                                     \
754:  *   devif_iob_poll(devif_poll_callback())  devif_poll_callback()
755:  *        /                                           \
756:  *       /                                             \
757:  *  devif_poll("NIC"_txpoll)                     "NIC"_send()(dev->d_buf)
758:  *
759:  ****************************************************************************/
760: 
761: int devif_poll(FAR struct net_driver_s *dev, devif_poll_callback_t callback);
762: 
763: /****************************************************************************
764:  * Name: neighbor_out
765:  *
766:  * Description:
767:  *   This function should be called before sending out an IPv6 packet. The
768:  *   function checks the destination IPv6 address of the IPv6 packet to see
769:  *   what L2 address that should be used as a destination L2 address.
770:  *
771:  *   If the destination IPv6 address is in the local network (determined
772:  *   by logical ANDing of netmask and our IPv6 address), the function
773:  *   checks the Neighbor Table to see if an entry for the destination IPv6
774:  *   address is found.  If so, an L2 header is pre-pended at the beginning
775:  *   of the packet and the function returns.
776:  *
777:  *   If no Neighbor Table entry is found for the destination IPv6 address,
778:  *   the packet in the d_buf is replaced by an ICMPv6 Neighbor Solicit
779:  *   request packet for the IPv6 address. The IPv6 packet is dropped and
780:  *   it is assumed that the higher level protocols (e.g., TCP) eventually
781:  *   will retransmit the dropped packet.
782:  *
783:  *   Upon return in either the case, a packet to be sent is present in the
784:  *   d_buf buffer and the d_len field holds the length of the L2 frame that
785:  *   should be transmitted.
786:  *
787:  ****************************************************************************/
788: 
789: #ifdef CONFIG_NET_IPv6
790: void neighbor_out(FAR struct net_driver_s *dev);
791: #endif /* CONFIG_NET_IPv6 */

105: #define SIOCGIWFRAG         _WLIOC(0x0025)  /* Get fragmentation thr (bytes) */

124: #define SIOCGIWGENIE        _WLIOC(0x0031)  /* Get generic IE */

145: /* -------------------- DEV PRIVATE IOCTL LIST -------------------- */
146: 
147: /* These 32 ioctl are wireless device private, for 16 commands.
148:  * Each driver is free to use them for whatever purpose it chooses,

438: /* Generic format for most parameters that fit in a int32_t */
439: 
440: struct iw_param
441: {
442:   int32_t   value;          /* The value of the parameter itself */
443:   uint8_t   fixed;          /* Hardware should not use auto select */
444:   uint8_t   disabled;       /* Disable the feature */
445:   uint16_t  flags;          /* Optional flags */
446: };
447: 
448: /* Large data reference.  For all data larger than 16 octets,
449:  * we need to use a pointer to memory allocated in user space.
450:  */
451: 
452: struct iw_point
453: {
454:   FAR void *pointer;        /* Pointer to the data  (in user space) */
455:   uint16_t  length;         /* number of fields or size in bytes */
456:   uint16_t  flags;          /* Optional flags */
457: };
458: 
459: /* For numbers lower than 10^9, we encode the number in 'm' and set 'e' to 0
460:  * For number greater than 10^9, we divide it by the lowest power of 10 to
461:  * get 'm' lower than 10^9, with 'm'= f / (10^'e')...
462:  * The power of 10 is in 'e', the result of the division is in 'm'.
463:  */
464: 
465: struct iw_freq
466: {
467:   int32_t   m;              /* Mantissa */
468:   int16_t   e;              /* Exponent */
469:   uint8_t   i;              /* List index (when in range struct) */
470:   uint8_t   flags;          /* Flags (fixed/auto) */
471: };

473: /* Quality of the link */
474: 
475: struct iw_quality
476: {
477:   uint8_t   qual;           /* link quality (retries, SNR,
478:                              * missed beacons or better...) */
479:   uint8_t   level;          /* signal level (dBm) */
480:   uint8_t   noise;          /* noise level (dBm) */
481:   uint8_t   updated;        /* Flags to know if updated */
482: };

484: /* Packet discarded in the wireless adapter due to
485:  * "wireless" specific problems...
486:  * Note : the list of counter and statistics in net_device_stats
487:  * is already pretty exhaustive, and you should use that first.
488:  * This is only additional stats...
489:  */
490: 
491: struct iw_discarded
492: {
493:   uint32_t nwid;      /* Rx : Wrong nwid/essid */
494:   uint32_t code;      /* Rx : Unable to code/decode (WEP) */
495:   uint32_t fragment;  /* Rx : Can't perform MAC reassembly */
496:   uint32_t retries;   /* Tx : Max MAC retries num reached */
497:   uint32_t misc;      /* Others cases */
498: };
499: 
500: /* Packet/Time period missed in the wireless adapter due to
501:  * "wireless" specific problems...
502:  */
503: 
504: struct iw_missed
505: {

507: };

509: /* This union defines the data payload of an ioctl
510:  * and is used in struct iwreq below.
511:  */
512: 
513: union iwreq_data
514: {
515:   char name[IFNAMSIZ];      /* Network interface name */
516:   struct iw_point essid;    /* Extended network name */
517:   struct iw_param nwid;     /* Network id (or domain - the cell) */
518:   struct iw_freq freq;      /* frequency or channel :
519:                              * 0-1000 = channel
520:                              * > 1000 = frequency in Hz */
521:   struct iw_param sens;     /* signal level threshold */
522:   struct iw_param bitrate;  /* default bit rate */
523:   struct iw_param txpower;  /* default transmit power */
524:   struct iw_param rts;      /* RTS threshold threshold */
525:   struct iw_param frag;     /* Fragmentation threshold */
526:   uint32_t mode;            /* Operation mode */
527:   struct iw_param retry;    /* Retry limits & lifetime */
528: 
529:   struct iw_point encoding; /* Encoding stuff : tokens */
530:   struct iw_param power;    /* PM duration/timeout */
531:   struct iw_quality qual;   /* Quality part of statistics */
532: 
533:   struct sockaddr ap_addr;  /* Access point address */
534:   struct sockaddr addr;     /* Destination address (hw/mac) */
535: 
536:   struct iw_param param;    /* Other small parameters */
537:   struct iw_point data;     /* Other large parameters */
538: };

541:  * This structure is the same as 'struct ifreq', but defined for
542:  * use with wireless IOCTLs.

556:   struct iw_freq freq[IW_MAX_FREQUENCIES];
557: };

564:   uint16_t           cmd;   /* Wireless IOCTL command */
565:   union iwreq_data   u;     /* Fixed IOCTL payload */
566: };

573:   uint8_t  tx_seq[IW_ENCODE_SEQ_MAX_SIZE]; /* LSB first */
574:   uint8_t  rx_seq[IW_ENCODE_SEQ_MAX_SIZE]; /* LSB first */
575:   struct sockaddr addr;                    /* ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff for
576:                                             * broadcast/multicast
577:                                             * (group) keys or unicast address
578:                                             * for individual keys */
579:   uint16_t alg;                            /* IW_ENCODE_ALG_* */
580:   uint16_t key_len;
581:   uint8_t  key[0];
582: };

584: /* Optional data for scan request
585:  *
586:  * Note: these optional parameters are controlling parameters for the
587:  * scanning behavior, these do not apply to getting scan results
588:  * (SIOCGIWSCAN). Drivers are expected to keep a local BSS table and
589:  * provide a merged results with all BSSes even if the previous scan
590:  * request limited scanning to a subset, e.g., by specifying an SSID.
591:  * Especially, scan results are required to include an entry for the
592:  * current BSS if the driver is in Managed mode and associated with an AP.
593:  */
594: 
595: struct  iw_scan_req
596: {
597:   uint8_t scan_type;     /* IW_SCAN_TYPE_{ACTIVE,PASSIVE} */
598:   uint8_t essid_len;
599:   uint8_t num_channels;  /* num entries in channel_list;
600:                           * 0 = scan all allowed channels */
601:   uint8_t flags;         /* reserved as padding; use zero, this may
602:                           * be used in the future for adding flags
603:                           * to request different scan behavior */
604:   struct sockaddr bssid; /* ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff for broadcast BSSID or
605:                           * individual address of a specific BSS */
606: 
607:   /* Use this ESSID if IW_SCAN_THIS_ESSID flag is used instead of using
608:    * the current ESSID. This allows scan requests for specific ESSID
609:    * without having to change the current ESSID and potentially breaking
610:    * the current association.
611:    */
612: 
613:   uint8_t essid[IW_ESSID_MAX_SIZE];
614: 
615:   /* Optional parameters for changing the default scanning behavior.
616:    * These are based on the MLME-SCAN.request from IEEE Std 802.11.
617:    * TU is 1.024 ms. If these are set to 0, driver is expected to use
618:    * reasonable default values. min_channel_time defines the time that
619:    * will be used to wait for the first reply on each channel. If no
620:    * replies are received, next channel will be scanned after this. If
621:    * replies are received, total time waited on the channel is defined by
622:    * max_channel_time.
623:    */
624: 
625:   uint32_t min_channel_time; /* in TU */
626:   uint32_t max_channel_time; /* in TU */
627: 
628:   struct iw_freq  channel_list[IW_MAX_FREQUENCIES];
629: };
630: 
631: /* Wireless statistics */
632: 
633: struct iw_statistics
634: {
635:   uint16_t status;              /* Status
636:                                  * - device dependent for now
637:                                  */
638: 
639:   struct iw_quality qual;       /* Quality of the link
640:                                  * (instant/mean/max)
641:                                  */
642:   struct iw_discarded discard;  /* Packet discarded counts */
643:   struct iw_missed miss;        /* Packet missed counts */
644: };

650:   (offsetof(struct iw_event, u) + sizeof(((union iwreq_data *)0)->field))

271: /* Note:
272:  *     All TX done/RX done/Error trigger functions are not called from
273:  *     interrupts, this is much different from ethernet driver, including:
274:  *       * wlan_rx_done
275:  *       * wlan_tx_done
276:  *
277:  *     These functions are called in a Wi-Fi private thread. So we just use
278:  *     mutex/semaphore instead of disable interrupt, if necessary.

281: /****************************************************************************
282:  * Function: wlan_cache_txpkt_tail
283:  *
284:  * Description:
285:  *   Cache packet from dev->d_buf into tail of TX ready queue.
286:  *
287:  * Input Parameters:
288:  *   priv - Reference to the driver state structure
289:  *
290:  * Returned Value:
291:  *   None
292:  *
293:  ****************************************************************************/
294: 
295: static inline void wlan_cache_txpkt_tail(struct wlan_priv_s *priv)
296: {
297:   if (priv->dev.d_iob)
298:     {
299:       iob_tryadd_queue(priv->dev.d_iob, &priv->txb);
300:     }
301: 
302:   netdev_iob_clear(&priv->dev);
303: }
304: 
305: /****************************************************************************
306:  * Function: wlan_recvframe
307:  *
308:  * Description:
309:  *   Try to receive RX packet from RX done packet queue.
310:  *
311:  * Input Parameters:
312:  *   priv - Reference to the driver state structure
313:  *
314:  * Returned Value:
315:  *   RX packet if success or NULl if no packet in queue.
316:  *
317:  ****************************************************************************/
318: 
319: static struct iob_s *wlan_recvframe(struct wlan_priv_s *priv)
320: {
321:   struct iob_s *iob;
322: 
323:   iob = iob_remove_queue(&priv->rxb);
324: 
325:   return iob;
326: }
327: 
328: /****************************************************************************
329:  * Name: wlan_transmit
330:  *
331:  * Description:
332:  *   Try to send all TX packets in TX ready queue to Wi-Fi driver. If this
333:  *    sending fails, then breaks loop and returns.
334:  *
335:  * Input Parameters:
336:  *   priv - Reference to the driver state structure
337:  *
338:  * Returned Value:
339:  *   None
340:  *
341:  ****************************************************************************/
342: 
343: static void wlan_transmit(struct wlan_priv_s *priv)
344: {
345:   uint16_t llhdrlen = NET_LL_HDRLEN(&priv->dev);
346:   unsigned int offset = CONFIG_NET_LL_GUARDSIZE - llhdrlen;
347:   struct iob_s *iob;
348:   int ret;
349: 
350:   while ((iob = iob_peek_queue(&priv->txb)) != NULL)
351:     {
352:       iob_copyout(priv->flatbuf + llhdrlen, iob, iob->io_pktlen, 0);
353:       memcpy(priv->flatbuf, iob->io_data + offset, llhdrlen);
354: 
355:       ret = priv->ops->send(priv->flatbuf, iob->io_pktlen + llhdrlen);
356:       if (ret == -ENOMEM)
357:         {
358:           wd_start(&priv->txtimeout, WLAN_TXTOUT,
359:                    wlan_txtimeout_expiry, (uint32_t)priv);
360:           break;
361:         }
362:       else
363:         {
364:           if (ret < 0)
365:             {
366:               nwarn("WARN: Failed to send pkt, ret: %d\n", ret);
367:             }
368: 
369:           iob_remove_queue(&priv->txb);
370: 
371:           /* And free the I/O buffer chain */
372: 
373:           iob_free_chain(iob);
374:         }
375:     }
376: }
377: 
378: /****************************************************************************
379:  * Name: wlan_tx_done
380:  *
381:  * Description:
382:  *   Wi-Fi TX done callback function. If this is called, it means sending
383:  *   next packet.
384:  *
385:  * Input Parameters:
386:  *   priv   - Reference to the driver state structure
387:  *
388:  * Returned Value:
389:  *   None
390:  *
391:  ****************************************************************************/
392: 
393: static void wlan_tx_done(struct wlan_priv_s *priv)
394: {
395:   wd_cancel(&priv->txtimeout);
396: 
397:   wlan_txavail(&priv->dev);
398: }

400: /****************************************************************************
401:  * Function: wlan_rx_done
402:  *
403:  * Description:
404:  *   Wi-Fi RX done callback function. If this is called, it means receiving
405:  *   packet.
406:  *
407:  * Input Parameters:
408:  *   priv   - Reference to the driver state structure
409:  *   buffer - Wi-Fi received packet buffer
410:  *   len    - Length of received packet
411:  *   eb     - Wi-Fi receive callback input eb pointer
412:  *
413:  * Returned Value:
414:  *   0 on success or a negated errno on failure
415:  *
416:  ****************************************************************************/
417: 
418: static int wlan_rx_done(struct wlan_priv_s *priv, void *buffer,
419:                         uint16_t len, void *eb)
420: {
421:   struct net_driver_s *dev = &priv->dev;
422:   struct iob_s *iob = NULL;
423:   irqstate_t flags;
424:   int ret = 0;
425: 
426:   if (!priv->ifup)
427:     {
428:       goto out;
429:     }
430: 
431:   if (len > WLAN_BUF_SIZE)
432:     {
433:       nwarn("ERROR: Wlan receive %d larger than %d\n",
434:              len, WLAN_BUF_SIZE);
435:       ret = -EINVAL;
436:       goto out;
437:     }
438: 
439:   if (len > iob_navail(false) * CONFIG_IOB_BUFSIZE)
440:     {
441:       ret = -ENOBUFS;
442:       goto out;
443:     }
444: 
445:   iob = iob_tryalloc(false);
446:   if (iob == NULL)
447:     {
448:       ret = -ENOBUFS;
449:       goto out;
450:     }
451: 
452:   iob_reserve(iob, CONFIG_NET_LL_GUARDSIZE - NET_LL_HDRLEN(dev));
453: 
454:   ret = iob_trycopyin(iob, buffer, len, 0, false);
455:   if (ret != len)
456:     {
457:       ret = -ENOBUFS;
458:       goto out;
459:     }
460: 
461:   flags = spin_lock_irqsave(&priv->lock);
462:   ret = iob_tryadd_queue(iob, &priv->rxb);
463:   spin_unlock_irqrestore(&priv->lock, flags);
464: 
465:   if (ret < 0)
466:     {
467:       ret = -ENOBUFS;
468:       goto out;
469:     }
470: 
471: out:
472: 
473:   if (eb != NULL)
474:     {
475:       esp_wifi_free_eb(eb);
476:     }
477: 
478:   if (ret != OK && iob != NULL)
479:     {
480:       iob_free_chain(iob);
481:     }
482: 
483:   if (work_available(&priv->rxwork))
484:     {
485:       work_queue(WLAN_WORK, &priv->rxwork, wlan_rxpoll, priv, 0);
486:     }
487: 
488:   wlan_txavail(&priv->dev);
489: 
490:   return ret;
491: }
492: 
493: /****************************************************************************
494:  * Function: wlan_rxpoll
495:  *
496:  * Description:
497:  *   Try to receive packets from RX done queue and pass packets into IP
498:  *   stack and send packets which is from IP stack if necessary.
499:  *
500:  * Input Parameters:
501:  *   priv - Reference to the driver state structure
502:  *
503:  * Returned Value:
504:  *   None
505:  *
506:  ****************************************************************************/
507: 
508: static void wlan_rxpoll(void *arg)
509: {
510:   struct wlan_priv_s *priv = (struct wlan_priv_s *)arg;
511:   struct net_driver_s *dev = &priv->dev;
512:   struct eth_hdr_s *eth_hdr;
513:   struct iob_s *iob;
514: 
515:   /* Try to send all cached TX packets for TX ack and so on */
516: 
517:   wlan_transmit(priv);
518: 
519:   /* Loop while while iob_remove_queue() successfully retrieves valid
520:    * Ethernet frames.
521:    */
522: 
523:   net_lock();
524: 
525:   while ((iob = wlan_recvframe(priv)) != NULL)
526:     {
527:       dev->d_iob = iob;
528:       dev->d_len = iob->io_pktlen;
529: 
530:       iob_reserve(iob, CONFIG_NET_LL_GUARDSIZE);
531: 
532: #ifdef CONFIG_NET_PKT
533: 
534:       /* When packet sockets are enabled,
535:        * feed the frame into the packet tap.
536:        */
537: 
538:       pkt_input(&priv->dev);
539: #endif
540: 
541:       eth_hdr = (struct eth_hdr_s *)
542:         &dev->d_iob->io_data[CONFIG_NET_LL_GUARDSIZE -
543:                              NET_LL_HDRLEN(dev)];
544: 
545:       /* We only accept IP packets of the configured type and ARP packets */
546: 
547: #ifdef CONFIG_NET_IPv4
548:       if (eth_hdr->type == HTONS(ETHTYPE_IP))
549:         {
550:           ninfo("IPv4 frame\n");
551: 
552:           /* Receive an IPv4 packet from the network device */
553: 
554:           ipv4_input(&priv->dev);
555: 
556:           /* If the above function invocation resulted in data
557:            * that should be sent out on the network,
558:            * the field  d_len will set to a value > 0.
559:            */
560: 
561:           if (priv->dev.d_len > 0)
562:             {
563:               /* And send the packet */
564: 
565:               wlan_cache_txpkt_tail(priv);
566:             }
567:         }
568:       else
569: #endif
570: #ifdef CONFIG_NET_IPv6
571:       if (eth_hdr->type == HTONS(ETHTYPE_IP6))
572:         {
573:           ninfo("IPv6 frame\n");
574: 
575:           /* Give the IPv6 packet to the network layer */
576: 
577:           ipv6_input(&priv->dev);
578: 
579:           /* If the above function invocation resulted in data
580:            * that should be sent out on the network, the field
581:            * d_len will set to a value > 0.
582:            */
583: 
584:           if (priv->dev.d_len > 0)
585:             {
586:               /* And send the packet */
587: 
588:               wlan_cache_txpkt_tail(priv);
589:             }
590:         }
591:       else
592: #endif
593: #ifdef CONFIG_NET_ARP
594:       if (eth_hdr->type == HTONS(ETHTYPE_ARP))
595:         {
596:           ninfo("ARP frame\n");
597: 
598:           /* Handle ARP packet */
599: 
600:           arp_input(&priv->dev);
601: 
602:           /* If the above function invocation resulted in data
603:            * that should be sent out on the network, the field
604:            * d_len will set to a value > 0.
605:            */
606: 
607:           if (priv->dev.d_len > 0)
608:             {
609:               wlan_cache_txpkt_tail(priv);
610:             }
611:         }
612:       else
613: #endif
614:         {
615:           ninfo("INFO: Dropped, Unknown type: %04x\n", eth_hdr->type);
616:         }
617: 
618:       netdev_iob_release(&priv->dev);
619:     }
620: 
621:   /* Try to send all cached TX packets */
622: 
623:   wlan_transmit(priv);
624: 
625:   net_unlock();
626: }

628: /****************************************************************************
629:  * Name: wlan_txpoll
630:  *
631:  * Description:
632:  *   The transmitter is available, check if the network has any outgoing
633:  *   packets ready to send.  This is a callback from devif_poll().
634:  *   devif_poll() may be called:
635:  *
636:  *   1. When the preceding TX packets send times out and the interface is
637:  *      reset
638:  *   2. During normal TX polling
639:  *
640:  * Input Parameters:
641:  *   dev - Reference to the NuttX driver state structure
642:  *
643:  * Returned Value:
644:  *   OK on success; a negated errno on failure
645:  *
646:  ****************************************************************************/
647: 
648: static int wlan_txpoll(struct net_driver_s *dev)
649: {
650:   struct wlan_priv_s *priv = dev->d_private;
651: 
652:   wlan_cache_txpkt_tail(priv);
653:   wlan_transmit(priv);
654: 
655:   return OK;
656: }
657: 
658: /****************************************************************************
659:  * Function: wlan_dopoll
660:  *
661:  * Description:
662:  *   The function is called in order to perform an out-of-sequence TX poll.
663:  *   This is done:
664:  *
665:  *   1. When new TX data is available (wlan_txavail)
666:  *   2. After a TX timeout to restart the sending process
667:  *      (wlan_txtimeout_expiry).
668:  *
669:  * Input Parameters:
670:  *   priv - Reference to the driver state structure
671:  *
672:  * Returned Value:
673:  *   None
674:  *
675:  ****************************************************************************/
676: 
677: static void wlan_dopoll(struct wlan_priv_s *priv)
678: {
679:   struct net_driver_s *dev = &priv->dev;
680: 
681:   /* Try to let TCP/IP to send all packets to netcard driver */
682: 
683:   while (devif_poll(dev, wlan_txpoll));
684: 
685:   /* Try to send all cached TX packets */
686: 
687:   wlan_transmit(priv);
688: }
689: 
690: /****************************************************************************
691:  * Function: wlan_txtimeout_work
692:  *
693:  * Description:
694:  *   Perform TX timeout related work from the worker thread
695:  *
696:  * Input Parameters:
697:  *   arg - The argument passed when work_queue() as called.
698:  *
699:  * Returned Value:
700:  *   OK on success
701:  *
702:  ****************************************************************************/
703: 
704: static void wlan_txtimeout_work(void *arg)
705: {
706:   struct wlan_priv_s *priv = (struct wlan_priv_s *)arg;
707: 
708:   /* Try to send all cached TX packets */
709: 
710:   wlan_transmit(priv);
711: 
712:   net_lock();
713: 
714:   wlan_ifdown(&priv->dev);
715:   wlan_ifup(&priv->dev);
716: 
717:   /* Then poll for new XMIT data */
718: 
719:   wlan_dopoll(priv);
720: 
721:   net_unlock();
722: }
723: 
724: /****************************************************************************
725:  * Function: wlan_txtimeout_expiry
726:  *
727:  * Description:
728:  *   Our TX watchdog timed out.  Called from the timer callback handler.
729:  *   The last TX never completed.  Reset the hardware and start again.
730:  *
731:  * Input Parameters:
732:  *   arg - The reference of the private driver structure
733:  *
734:  * Returned Value:
735:  *   None
736:  *
737:  ****************************************************************************/
738: 
739: static void wlan_txtimeout_expiry(wdparm_t arg)
740: {
741:   struct wlan_priv_s *priv = (struct wlan_priv_s *)arg;
742: 
743:   /* Schedule to perform the TX timeout processing on the worker thread. */
744: 
745:   if (work_available(&priv->toutwork))
746:     {
747:       work_queue(WLAN_WORK, &priv->toutwork, wlan_txtimeout_work, priv, 0);
748:     }
749: }
750: 
751: /****************************************************************************
752:  * Name: wlan_txavail_work
753:  *
754:  * Description:
755:  *   Perform an out-of-cycle poll on the worker thread.
756:  *
757:  * Input Parameters:
758:  *   arg - Reference to the NuttX driver state structure (cast to void*)
759:  *
760:  * Returned Value:
761:  *   None
762:  *
763:  * Assumptions:
764:  *   Called on the higher priority worker thread.
765:  *
766:  ****************************************************************************/
767: 
768: static void wlan_txavail_work(void *arg)
769: {
770:   struct wlan_priv_s *priv = (struct wlan_priv_s *)arg;
771: 
772:   /* Try to send all cached TX packets even if net is down */
773: 
774:   wlan_transmit(priv);
775: 
776:   /* Lock the network and serialize driver operations if necessary.
777:    * NOTE: Serialization is only required in the case where the driver work
778:    * is performed on an LP worker thread and where more than one LP worker
779:    * thread has been configured.
780:    */
781: 
782:   net_lock();
783: 
784:   /* Ignore the notification if the interface is not yet up */
785: 
786:   if (priv->ifup)
787:     {
788:       /* Poll the network for new XMIT data */
789: 
790:       wlan_dopoll(priv);
791:     }
792: 
793:   net_unlock();
794: }

796: /****************************************************************************
797:  * Name: wlan_ifup
798:  *
799:  * Description:
800:  *   NuttX Callback: Bring up the Ethernet interface when an IP address is
801:  *   provided
802:  *
803:  * Input Parameters:
804:  *   dev - Reference to the NuttX driver state structure
805:  *
806:  * Returned Value:
807:  *   None
808:  *
809:  ****************************************************************************/
810: 
811: static int wlan_ifup(struct net_driver_s *dev)
812: {
813:   int ret;
814:   struct wlan_priv_s *priv = (struct wlan_priv_s *)dev->d_private;
815: 
816: #ifdef CONFIG_NET_IPv4
817:   ninfo("Bringing up: %u.%u.%u.%u\n",
818:         ip4_addr1(dev->d_ipaddr), ip4_addr2(dev->d_ipaddr),
819:         ip4_addr3(dev->d_ipaddr), ip4_addr4(dev->d_ipaddr));
820: #endif
821: #ifdef CONFIG_NET_IPv6
822:   ninfo("Bringing up: %04x:%04x:%04x:%04x:%04x:%04x:%04x:%04x\n",
823:         dev->d_ipv6addr[0], dev->d_ipv6addr[1], dev->d_ipv6addr[2],
824:         dev->d_ipv6addr[3], dev->d_ipv6addr[4], dev->d_ipv6addr[5],
825:         dev->d_ipv6addr[6], dev->d_ipv6addr[7]);
826: #endif
827: 
828:   net_lock();
829: 
830:   if (priv->ifup)
831:     {
832:       net_unlock();
833:       return OK;
834:     }
835: 
836:   ret = priv->ops->start();
837:   if (ret < 0)
838:     {
839:       net_unlock();
840:       nerr("ERROR: Failed to start Wi-Fi ret=%d\n", ret);
841:       return ret;
842:     }
843: 
844:   IOB_QINIT(&priv->rxb);
845:   IOB_QINIT(&priv->txb);
846: 
847:   priv->dev.d_buf = NULL;
848:   priv->dev.d_len = 0;
849: 
850:   priv->ifup = true;
851:   if (g_callback_register_ref == 0)
852:     {
853:       ret = esp_register_shutdown_handler(esp_wifi_stop_callback);
854:       if (ret < 0)
855:         {
856:           nwarn("WARN: Failed to register handler ret=%d\n", ret);
857:         }
858:     }
859: 
860:   ++g_callback_register_ref;
861:   net_unlock();
862: 
863:   return OK;
864: }
865: 
866: /****************************************************************************
867:  * Name: wlan_ifdown
868:  *
869:  * Description:
870:  *   NuttX Callback: Stop the interface.
871:  *
872:  * Input Parameters:
873:  *   dev - Reference to the NuttX driver state structure
874:  *
875:  * Returned Value:
876:  *   None
877:  *
878:  ****************************************************************************/
879: 
880: static int wlan_ifdown(struct net_driver_s *dev)
881: {
882:   int ret;
883:   struct wlan_priv_s *priv = (struct wlan_priv_s *)dev->d_private;
884: 
885:   net_lock();
886: 
887:   if (!priv->ifup)
888:     {
889:       net_unlock();
890:       return OK;
891:     }
892: 
893:   /* Cancel the TX poll timer and TX timeout timers */
894: 
895:   wd_cancel(&priv->txtimeout);
896: 
897:   /* Mark the device "down" */
898: 
899:   priv->ifup = false;
900: 
901:   iob_free_queue(&priv->rxb);
902:   iob_free_queue(&priv->txb);
903: 
904:   ret = priv->ops->stop();
905:   if (ret < 0)
906:     {
907:       nerr("ERROR: Failed to stop Wi-Fi ret=%d\n", ret);
908:     }
909: 
910:   --g_callback_register_ref;
911:   if (g_callback_register_ref == 0)
912:     {
913:       ret = esp_unregister_shutdown_handler(esp_wifi_stop_callback);
914:       if (ret < 0)
915:         {
916:           nwarn("WARN: Failed to unregister handler ret=%d\n", ret);
917:         }
918:     }
919: 
920:   net_unlock();
921: 
922:   return OK;
923: }
924: 
925: /****************************************************************************
926:  * Name: wlan_txavail
927:  *
928:  * Description:
929:  *   Driver callback invoked when new TX data is available.  This is a
930:  *   stimulus perform an out-of-cycle poll and, thereby, reduce the TX
931:  *   latency.
932:  *
933:  * Input Parameters:
934:  *   dev - Reference to the NuttX driver state structure
935:  *
936:  * Returned Value:
937:  *   None
938:  *
939:  * Assumptions:
940:  *   Called in normal user mode
941:  *
942:  ****************************************************************************/
943: 
944: static int wlan_txavail(struct net_driver_s *dev)
945: {
946:   struct wlan_priv_s *priv = (struct wlan_priv_s *)dev->d_private;
947: 
948:   if (work_available(&priv->txwork))
949:     {
950:       /* Schedule to serialize the poll on the worker thread. */
951: 
952:       work_queue(WLAN_WORK, &priv->txwork, wlan_txavail_work, priv, 0);
953:     }
954: 
955:   return OK;
956: }

958: /****************************************************************************
959:  * Name: wlan_addmac
960:  *
961:  * Description:
962:  *   NuttX Callback: Add the specified MAC address to the hardware multicast
963:  *   address filtering
964:  *
965:  * Input Parameters:
966:  *   dev  - Reference to the NuttX driver state structure
967:  *   mac  - The MAC address to be added
968:  *
969:  * Returned Value:
970:  *   None
971:  *
972:  ****************************************************************************/
973: 
974: #if defined(CONFIG_NET_MCASTGROUP) || defined(CONFIG_NET_ICMPv6)

1012: /****************************************************************************
1013:  * Name: wlan_ioctl
1014:  *
1015:  * Description:
1016:  *   Handle network IOCTL commands directed to this device.
1017:  *
1018:  * Input Parameters:
1019:  *   dev - Reference to the NuttX driver state structure
1020:  *   cmd - The IOCTL command
1021:  *   arg - The argument for the IOCTL command
1022:  *
1023:  * Returned Value:
1024:  *   OK on success; Negated errno on failure.
1025:  *
1026:  ****************************************************************************/
1027: 
1028: #ifdef CONFIG_NETDEV_IOCTL
1029: static int wlan_ioctl(struct net_driver_s *dev,
1030:                       int cmd,
1031:                       unsigned long arg)
1032: {
1033:   int ret;
1034:   struct iwreq *iwr = (struct iwreq *)arg;
1035:   struct wlan_priv_s *priv = (struct wlan_priv_s *)dev->d_private;
1036:   const struct wlan_ops *ops = priv->ops;
1037: 
1038:   /* Decode and dispatch the driver-specific IOCTL command */
1039: 
1040:   switch (cmd)
1041:     {
1042: #ifdef CONFIG_NETDEV_PHY_IOCTL
1043: #ifdef CONFIG_ARCH_PHY_INTERRUPT
1044:       case SIOCMIINOTIFY: /* Set up for PHY event notifications */
1045:         {
1046:           struct mii_ioctl_notify_s *req = (struct mii_ioctl_notify_s *)arg;
1047:           ret = ops->event(req->pid, &req->event);
1048:           if (ret < 0)
1049:             {
1050:               nerr("ERROR: Failed to subscribe event\n");
1051:             }
1052:         }
1053:         break;
1054: #endif
1055: #endif
1056: 
1057:       case SIOCSIWENCODEEXT:
1058:         ret = ops->passwd(iwr, true);
1059: 
1060:         break;
1061: 
1062:       case SIOCGIWENCODEEXT:
1063:         ret = ops->passwd(iwr, false);
1064:         break;
1065: 
1066:       case SIOCSIWESSID:
1067:         if ((iwr->u.essid.flags == IW_ESSID_ON) ||
1068:             (iwr->u.essid.flags == IW_ESSID_DELAY_ON))
1069:           {
1070:             ret = ops->essid(iwr, true);
1071:             if (ret < 0)
1072:               {
1073:                 break;
1074:               }
1075: 
1076:             if (iwr->u.essid.flags == IW_ESSID_ON)
1077:               {
1078:                 ret = ops->connect();
1079:                 if (ret < 0)
1080:                   {
1081:                     nerr("ERROR: Failed to connect\n");
1082:                     break;
1083:                   }
1084:               }
1085:           }
1086:         else
1087:           {
1088:             ret = ops->disconnect();
1089:             if (ret < 0)
1090:               {
1091:                 nerr("ERROR: Failed to disconnect\n");
1092:                 break;
1093:               }
1094:           }
1095: 
1096:         break;
1097: 
1098:       case SIOCGIWESSID:    /* Get ESSID */
1099:         ret = ops->essid(iwr, false);
1100:         break;
1101: 
1102:       case SIOCSIWAP:       /* Set access point MAC addresses */
1103:         if (iwr->u.ap_addr.sa_data[0] != 0 &&
1104:             iwr->u.ap_addr.sa_data[1] != 0 &&
1105:             iwr->u.ap_addr.sa_data[2] != 0)
1106:           {
1107:             ret = ops->bssid(iwr, true);
1108:             if (ret < 0)
1109:               {
1110:                 nerr("ERROR: Failed to set BSSID\n");
1111:                 break;
1112:               }
1113: 
1114:             ret = ops->connect();
1115:             if (ret < 0)
1116:               {
1117:                 nerr("ERROR: Failed to connect\n");
1118:                 break;
1119:               }
1120:           }
1121:         else
1122:           {
1123:             ret = ops->disconnect();
1124:             if (ret < 0)
1125:               {
1126:                 nerr("ERROR: Failed to disconnect\n");
1127:                 break;
1128:               }
1129:           }
1130: 
1131:         break;
1132: 
1133:       case SIOCGIWAP:       /* Get access point MAC addresses */
1134:         ret = ops->bssid(iwr, false);
1135:         break;
1136: 
1137:       case SIOCSIWSCAN:
1138:         ret = esp_wifi_start_scan(iwr);
1139:         break;
1140: 
1141:       case SIOCGIWSCAN:
1142:         ret = esp_wifi_get_scan_results(iwr);
1143:         break;
1144: 
1145:       case SIOCSIWCOUNTRY:  /* Set country code */
1146:         ret = ops->country(iwr, true);
1147:         break;
1148: 
1149:       case SIOCGIWSENS:    /* Get sensitivity (dBm) */
1150:         ret = ops->rssi(iwr, false);
1151:         break;
1152: 
1153:       case SIOCSIWMODE:     /* Set operation mode */
1154:         ret = ops->mode(iwr, true);
1155:         break;
1156: 
1157:       case SIOCGIWMODE:     /* Get operation mode */
1158:         ret = ops->mode(iwr, false);
1159:         break;
1160: 
1161:       case SIOCSIWAUTH:    /* Set authentication mode params */
1162:         ret = ops->auth(iwr, true);
1163:         break;
1164: 
1165:       case SIOCGIWAUTH:    /* Get authentication mode params */
1166:         ret = ops->auth(iwr, false);
1167:         break;
1168: 
1169:       case SIOCSIWFREQ:     /* Set channel/frequency (MHz) */
1170:         ret = ops->freq(iwr, true);
1171:         break;
1172: 
1173:       case SIOCGIWFREQ:     /* Get channel/frequency (MHz) */
1174:         ret = ops->freq(iwr, false);
1175:         break;
1176: 
1177:       case SIOCSIWRATE:     /* Set default bit rate (Mbps) */
1178:         wlwarn("WARNING: SIOCSIWRATE not implemented\n");
1179:         ret = -ENOSYS;
1180:         break;
1181: 
1182:       case SIOCGIWRATE:     /* Get default bit rate (Mbps) */
1183:         ret = ops->bitrate(iwr, false);
1184:         break;
1185: 
1186:       case SIOCSIWTXPOW:    /* Set transmit power (dBm) */
1187:         ret = ops->txpower(iwr, true);
1188:         break;
1189: 
1190:       case SIOCGIWTXPOW:    /* Get transmit power (dBm) */
1191:         ret = ops->txpower(iwr, false);
1192:         break;
1193: 
1194:       case SIOCGIWRANGE:    /* Get range of parameters */
1195:         ret = ops->channel(iwr, false);
1196:         break;
1197: 
1198:       default:
1199:         nerr("ERROR: Unrecognized IOCTL command: %d\n", cmd);
1200:         ret = -ENOTTY;  /* Special return value for this case */
1201:         break;
1202:     }
1203: 
1204:   return ret;
1205: }
1206: #endif /* CONFIG_NETDEV_IOCTL */

1208: /****************************************************************************
1209:  * Name: esp_net_initialize
1210:  *
1211:  * Description:
1212:  *   Initialize the network driver.
1213:  *
1214:  * Input Parameters:
1215:  *   devno    - The device number.
1216:  *   mac_addr - MAC address.
1217:  *   ops      - A pointer to the structure containing the WLAN operations
1218:  *              functions.
1219:  *
1220:  * Returned Value:
1221:  *   OK on success; Negated errno on failure.
1222:  *
1223:  ****************************************************************************/
1224: 
1225: static int esp_net_initialize(int devno, uint8_t *mac_addr,
1226:                               const struct wlan_ops *ops)
1227: {
1228:   int ret;
1229:   struct wlan_priv_s *priv;
1230:   struct net_driver_s *netdev;
1231: 
1232:   priv = &g_wlan_priv[devno];
1233:   if (priv->ref)
1234:     {
1235:       priv->ref++;
1236:       return OK;
1237:     }
1238: 
1239:   netdev = &priv->dev;
1240: 
1241:   /* Initialize the driver structure */
1242: 
1243:   memset(priv, 0, sizeof(struct wlan_priv_s));
1244: 
1245:   netdev->d_ifup    = wlan_ifup;     /* I/F down callback */
1246:   netdev->d_ifdown  = wlan_ifdown;   /* I/F up (new IP address) callback */
1247:   netdev->d_txavail = wlan_txavail;  /* New TX data callback */
1248: #ifdef CONFIG_NET_MCASTGROUP
1249:   netdev->d_addmac  = wlan_addmac;   /* Add multicast MAC address */
1250:   netdev->d_rmmac   = wlan_rmmac;    /* Remove multicast MAC address */
1251: #endif
1252: #ifdef CONFIG_NETDEV_IOCTL
1253:   netdev->d_ioctl   = wlan_ioctl;    /* Handle network IOCTL commands */
1254: #endif
1255: 
1256:   /* Used to recover private state from dev */
1257: 
1258:   netdev->d_private = (void *)priv;
1259: 
1260:   memcpy(netdev->d_mac.ether.ether_addr_octet, mac_addr, MAC_LEN);
1261: 
1262:   ret = netdev_register(netdev, NET_LL_IEEE80211);
1263:   if (ret < 0)
1264:     {
1265:       nerr("ERROR: Initialization of IEEE 802.11 block failed: %d\n", ret);
1266:       return ret;
1267:     }
1268: 
1269:   priv->ops = ops;
1270: 
1271:   priv->ref++;
1272: 
1273:   ninfo("INFO: Initialize Wi-Fi adapter No.%d success\n", devno);
1274: 
1275:   return OK;
1276: }

111: /****************************************************************************
112:  * Name: quota_is_valid
113:  *
114:  * Description:
115:  *   Check if the quota of the lower half is not too big.
116:  *
117:  ****************************************************************************/
118: 
119: static bool quota_is_valid(FAR struct netdev_lowerhalf_s *lower)
120: {
121:   int total = 0;
122:   enum netpkt_type_e type;
123: 
124:   for (type = NETPKT_TX; type < NETPKT_TYPENUM; type++)
125:     {
126:       total += netdev_lower_quota_load(lower, type);
127:     }
128: 
129:   if (total > NETPKT_BUFNUM)
130:     {
131:       nerr("ERROR: Too big quota when registering device: %d\n", total);
132:       return false;
133:     }
134: 
135:   if (total > NETPKT_BUFNUM / 2)
136:     {
137:       nwarn("WARNING: The quota of the registering device may consume more "
138:             "than half of the network buffers, which may hurt performance. "
139:             "Please consider decreasing driver quota or increasing nIOB.\n");
140:     }
141: 
142:   return true;
143: }

145: /****************************************************************************
146:  * Name: netpkt_get
147:  *
148:  * Description:
149:  *   Wraps the d_iob of dev to a netpkt.
150:  *

152:  *   Called with the network locked.

156: static FAR netpkt_t *netpkt_get(FAR struct net_driver_s *dev,
157:                                 enum netpkt_type_e type)
158: {
159:   FAR struct netdev_upperhalf_s *upper;
160:   FAR netpkt_t *pkt;
161: 
162:   DEBUGASSERT(dev && dev->d_iob);
163: 
164:   upper = (FAR struct netdev_upperhalf_s *)dev->d_private;
165:   pkt = dev->d_iob;
166: 
167:   netdev_iob_clear(dev);
168: 
169:   /* Do not limit quota here (simply relay iob instead of dropping), most
170:    * cases will be limited by netdev_upper_can_tx and seldom reaches here.
171:    */
172: 
173:   if (atomic_sub(&upper->lower->quota_ptr[type], 1) <= 0)
174:     {
175:       nwarn("WARNING: Allowing temperarily exceeding quota of %s.\n",
176:             dev->d_ifname);
177:     }
178: 
179:   return pkt;

234: /****************************************************************************
235:  * Name: netdev_upper_can_tx
236:  *
237:  * Description:
238:  *   Check if we allow tx on this device.
239:  *
240:  * Assumptions:
241:  *   Called with the network locked.
242:  *
243:  ****************************************************************************/
244: 
245: static inline bool netdev_upper_can_tx(FAR struct netdev_upperhalf_s *upper)
246: {
247:   FAR struct netdev_lowerhalf_s *lower = upper->lower;
248:   int quota = netdev_lower_quota_load(lower, NETPKT_TX);
249: 
250:   if (quota <= 0 && lower->ops->reclaim)
251:     {
252:       lower->ops->reclaim(lower);
253:       quota = netdev_lower_quota_load(lower, NETPKT_TX);
254:     }
255: 
256:   return quota > 0;
257: }

259: /****************************************************************************
260:  * Name: netdev_upper_txpoll
261:  *
262:  * Description:
263:  *   The transmitter is available, check if the network has any outgoing
264:  *   packets ready to send.  This is a callback from devif_poll().
265:  *   devif_poll() may be called:
266:  *
267:  *   1. When the preceding TX packet send is complete
268:  *   2. When the preceding TX packet send times out and the interface is
269:  *      reset
270:  *   3. During normal TX polling
271:  *
272:  * Input Parameters:
273:  *   dev - Reference to the NuttX driver state structure
274:  *
275:  * Returned Value:
276:  *   Negated errno value - Error number that occurs.
277:  *   NETDEV_TX_CONTINUE  - Driver can send more, continue the poll.
278:  *
279:  * Assumptions:
280:  *   Called with the network locked.
281:  *
282:  ****************************************************************************/
283: 
284: static int netdev_upper_txpoll(FAR struct net_driver_s *dev)
285: {
286:   FAR struct netdev_upperhalf_s *upper = dev->d_private;
287:   FAR struct netdev_lowerhalf_s *lower = upper->lower;
288:   FAR netpkt_t                  *pkt;
289:   int                            ret;
290: 
291:   DEBUGASSERT(dev->d_len > 0);
292: 
293:   NETDEV_TXPACKETS(dev);
294: 
295: #ifdef CONFIG_NET_PKT
296:   /* When packet sockets are enabled, loopback the tx frame to pkt socket
297:    * who has protocl type of ETH_P_ALL
298:    */
299: 
300:   pkt_loopback(dev);
301: #endif
302: 
303:   pkt = netpkt_get(dev, NETPKT_TX);
304: 
305:   if (netpkt_getdatalen(lower, pkt) > NETDEV_PKTSIZE(dev))
306:     {
307:       nerr("ERROR: Packet too long to send!\n");
308:       ret = -EMSGSIZE;
309:     }
310:   else
311:     {
312:       ret = lower->ops->transmit(lower, pkt);
313:     }
314: 
315:   if (ret != OK)
316:     {
317:       /* Stop polling on any error
318:        * REVISIT: maybe store the pkt in upper half and retry later?
319:        */
320: 
321:       NETDEV_TXERRORS(dev);
322:       nerr("ERROR: Transmit failed: %d\n", ret);
323:       netpkt_put(dev, pkt, NETPKT_TX);
324:       return ret;
325:     }
326: 
327:   return NETDEV_TX_CONTINUE;
328: }

330: /****************************************************************************
331:  * Name: netdev_upper_tx
332:  *
333:  * Description:
334:  *   Do the actual transmission of packets, including pre-queued packets and
335:  *   packets from the network stack.
336:  *
337:  * Input Parameters:
338:  *   dev - Reference to the NuttX driver state structure
339:  *
340:  * Returned Value:
341:  *   Negated errno value - Error number that occurs.
342:  *   NETDEV_TX_CONTINUE  - Driver can send more, continue the poll.
343:  *
344:  * Assumptions:
345:  *   Called with the network locked.
346:  *
347:  ****************************************************************************/
348: 
349: static int netdev_upper_tx(FAR struct net_driver_s *dev)
350: {
351: #if CONFIG_IOB_NCHAINS > 0
352:   FAR struct netdev_upperhalf_s *upper = dev->d_private;
353: 
354:   if (!IOB_QEMPTY(&upper->txq))
355:     {
356:       /* Put the packet back to the device */
357: 
358:       netdev_iob_replace_l2(dev, iob_remove_queue(&upper->txq));
359:       return netdev_upper_txpoll(dev);
360:     }
361: #endif
362: 
363:   /* No more TX packets in queue, poll the net stack to get more packets */
364: 
365:   return devif_poll(dev, netdev_upper_txpoll);
366: }

368: /****************************************************************************
369:  * Name: netdev_upper_txavail_work
370:  *
371:  * Description:
372:  *   Perform an out-of-cycle tx poll on the worker thread.
373:  *
374:  * Input Parameters:
375:  *   upper - Reference to the upper half driver structure
376:  *
377:  * Assumptions:
378:  *   Called with the network locked.
379:  *
380:  ****************************************************************************/
381: 
382: static void netdev_upper_txavail_work(FAR struct netdev_upperhalf_s *upper)
383: {
384:   FAR struct net_driver_s *dev = &upper->lower->netdev;
385: 
386:   /* Ignore the notification if the interface is not yet up */
387: 
388:   netdev_lock(dev);
389:   if (IFF_IS_UP(dev->d_flags) && !upper->txing)
390:     {
391:       DEBUGASSERT(dev->d_buf == NULL); /* Make sure: IOB only. */
392:       upper->txing = true;
393:       while (netdev_upper_can_tx(upper) &&
394:              netdev_upper_tx(dev) == NETDEV_TX_CONTINUE);
395:       upper->txing = false;
396:     }
397: 
398:   netdev_unlock(dev);
399: }

406:  *
407:  * Input Parameters:
408:  *   dev - Reference to the NuttX driver state structure
409:  *

411:  *   Called with the network locked.
412:  *

415: #if defined(CONFIG_NET_LOOPBACK) || defined(CONFIG_NET_ETHERNET) || \
416:     defined(CONFIG_DRIVERS_IEEE80211) || defined(CONFIG_NET_MBIM)
417: static void netdev_upper_queue_tx(FAR struct net_driver_s *dev)

419: #if CONFIG_IOB_NCHAINS > 0

423:   if ((ret = iob_tryadd_queue(dev->d_iob, &upper->txq)) >= 0)

426:       netdev_upper_txavail(dev);

428:   else

430:       nwarn("WARNING: Failed to queue TX packet, dropping: %d\n", ret);
431:     }
432: #else
433:   /* Fall back to send the packet directly if we don't have IOB queue. */
434: 
435:   netdev_upper_txpoll(dev);
436: #endif
437: }

900:  *   Handle upper layer ethtool IOCTL commands for a network device.
901:  *   This function processes ethtool-related IOCTL requests that are handled
902:  *   at the upper network layer, interacting with the specified network
903:  *   device.
904:  *
905:  * Input Parameters:
906:  *   dev - Pointer to the network driver structure (struct net_driver_s)
907:  *         representing the network device to operate on.
908:  *   arg - IOCTL command argument. The specific type and interpretation
909:  *         depend on the ethtool command being processed (e.g., may point to
910:  *         an struct ethtool_cmd or other ethtool-related data structure).
911:  *
912:  * Returned Value:
913:  *   On success, returns 0.
914:  *   On failure, returns a negative error code.
915:  ****************************************************************************/
916: 
917: #ifdef CONFIG_NETDEV_ETHTOOL_IOCTL
918: static int netdev_upper_ethtool_ioctl(FAR struct net_driver_s *dev,
919:                                       unsigned long arg)
920: {
921:   FAR struct netdev_upperhalf_s *upper = dev->d_private;
922:   FAR struct netdev_lowerhalf_s *lower = upper->lower;
923:   uint32_t cmd = *(FAR const uint32_t *)arg;
924:   int ret = -EOPNOTSUPP;
925: 
926:   switch (cmd)
927:     {
928:       case ETHTOOL_GCHANNELS:
929:         if (lower->eth_ops->get_channels)
930:           {
931:             ret = lower->eth_ops->get_channels(lower,
932:                                   (FAR struct ethtool_chns *)arg);
933:           }
934:         break;
935: 
936:       case ETHTOOL_SCHANNELS:
937:         if (lower->eth_ops->set_channels)
938:           {
939:             ret = lower->eth_ops->set_channels(lower,
940:                                   (FAR struct ethtool_chns *)arg);
941:           }
942:         break;
943: 
944:       case ETHTOOL_GCHANNELS2:
945:         if (lower->eth_ops->get_channels2)
946:           {
947:             ret = lower->eth_ops->get_channels2(lower,
948:                                   (FAR struct ethtool_chns2 *)arg);
949:           }
950:         break;
951: 
952:       case ETHTOOL_SCHANNELS2:
953:         if (lower->eth_ops->set_channels2)
954:           {
955:             ret = lower->eth_ops->set_channels2(lower,
956:                                   (FAR struct ethtool_chns2 *)arg);
957:           }
958:         break;
959: 
960:       default:
961:         ret = -ENOTTY;
962:         nerr("ERROR: No such cmd in ethtool opt!");
963:         break;
964:     }
965: 
966:   return ret;
967: }
968: #endif

971:  * Name: netdev_upper_wireless_ioctl

978: #ifdef CONFIG_NETDEV_WIRELESS_HANDLER
979: int netdev_upper_wireless_ioctl(FAR struct netdev_lowerhalf_s *lower,
980:                                 int cmd, unsigned long arg)
981: {
982:   int ret = -ENOTTY; /* Default to ENOTTY to indicate not serving. */
983:   FAR struct iwreq *iwr = (FAR struct iwreq *)arg;
984:   FAR const struct wireless_ops_s *ops = lower->iw_ops;
985:   struct ether_addr zero;
986: 
987:   /* Decode and dispatch the driver-specific IOCTL command */
988: 
989:   switch (cmd)
990:     {
991:       case SIOCSIWENCODEEXT: /* Set encoding token & mode */
992:         if (ops->passwd)
993:           {
994:             ret = ops->passwd(lower, iwr, true);
995:           }
996:         break;
997: 
998:       case SIOCGIWENCODEEXT: /* Get encoding token & mode */
999:         if (ops->passwd)
1000:           {
1001:             ret = ops->passwd(lower, iwr, false);
1002:           }
1003:         break;
1004: 
1005:       case SIOCSIWESSID: /* Set ESSID */
1006:         if (ops->essid)
1007:           {
1008:             if ((iwr->u.essid.flags == IW_ESSID_ON) ||
1009:                 (iwr->u.essid.flags == IW_ESSID_DELAY_ON))
1010:               {
1011:                 ret = ops->essid(lower, iwr, true);
1012:                 if (ret < 0)
1013:                   {
1014:                     break;
1015:                   }
1016: 
1017:                 if (iwr->u.essid.flags == IW_ESSID_ON)
1018:                   {
1019:                     ret = ops->connect(lower);
1020:                     if (ret < 0)
1021:                       {
1022:                         nerr("ERROR: Failed to connect\n");
1023:                         break;
1024:                       }
1025:                   }
1026:               }
1027:             else
1028:               {
1029:                 ret = ops->disconnect(lower);
1030:                 if (ret < 0)
1031:                   {
1032:                     nerr("ERROR: Failed to disconnect\n");
1033:                     break;
1034:                   }
1035:               }
1036:           }
1037:         break;
1038: 
1039:       case SIOCGIWESSID: /* Get ESSID */
1040:         if (ops->essid)
1041:           {
1042:             ret = ops->essid(lower, iwr, false);
1043:           }
1044:         break;
1045: 
1046:       case SIOCSIWAP: /* Set access point MAC addresses */
1047:         if (ops->bssid)
1048:           {
1049:             memset(&zero, 0, sizeof(zero));
1050:             if (memcmp(iwr->u.ap_addr.sa_data, &zero, sizeof(zero)) != 0)
1051:               {
1052:                 ret = ops->bssid(lower, iwr, true);
1053:                 if (ret < 0)
1054:                   {
1055:                     nerr("ERROR: Failed to set BSSID\n");
1056:                     break;
1057:                   }
1058: 
1059:                 ret = ops->connect(lower);
1060:                 if (ret < 0)
1061:                   {
1062:                     nerr("ERROR: Failed to connect\n");
1063:                     break;
1064:                   }
1065:               }
1066:             else
1067:               {
1068:                 ret = ops->disconnect(lower);
1069:                 if (ret < 0)
1070:                   {
1071:                     nerr("ERROR: Failed to disconnect\n");
1072:                     break;
1073:                   }

1260:     {
1261:       case NETDEV_RX_THREAD_RSS:

35: /****************************************************************************
36:  * Pre-processor Definitions

38: 
39: /* These are the register definitions for the OpenCores Ethernet MAC. */
40: 
41: /* DMA buffers configuration */
42: #define DMA_BUF_SIZE 1600
43: 
44: /* Only need 1 TX buf because packets are transmitted immediately */
45: #define TX_BUF_COUNT 1
46: 
47: /* This driver uses the interrupt source number of the internal EMAC
48:  * of the ESP32 chip, and uses the same register address base. This of
49:  * course only works in QEMU, where the OpenCores MAC is mapped to the
50:  * same register base and to the same interrupt source. This driver does
51:  * a sanity check that it is not running on the real ESP32 chip, using
52:  * the EMAC date register.
53:  */
54: #define OPENETH_BASE DR_REG_EMAC_BASE
55: 
56: /* OpenCores ethmac registers */
57: #define OPENETH_MODER_REG (OPENETH_BASE + 0x00)
58: #define OPENETH_MODER_DEFAULT 0xa000
59: /* OPENETH_RST: reset the MAC */
60: #define OPENETH_RST BIT(11)
61: /* OPENETH_PRO: enable promiscuous mode */
62: #define OPENETH_PRO BIT(5)
63: /*  OPENETH_TXEN: enable transmit */
64: #define OPENETH_TXEN BIT(1)
65: /*  OPENETH_RXEN: enable receive */
66: #define OPENETH_RXEN BIT(0)
67: 
68: #define OPENETH_INT_SOURCE_REG (OPENETH_BASE + 0x04)
69: #define OPENETH_INT_MASK_REG (OPENETH_BASE + 0x08)
70: /*  These bits apply to INT_SOURCE and INT_MASK registers: */
71: 
72: /*  OPENETH_INT_BUSY: Buffer was received and discarded due
73:  * to lack of buffers
74:  */
75: #define OPENETH_INT_BUSY BIT(4)
76: /*  OPENETH_INT_RXB: Frame received */
77: #define OPENETH_INT_RXB BIT(2)
78: /*  COLLCONF is not implemented in QEMU */
79: #define OPENETH_TX_BD_NUM_REG (OPENETH_BASE + 0x20)
80: /*  OPENETH_MAC_ADDR0_REG: bytes 2-5 of the MAC address (byte 5 in LSB) */
81: #define OPENETH_MAC_ADDR0_REG (OPENETH_BASE + 0x40)
82: /*  OPENETH_MAC_ADDR1_REG: bytes 0-1 of the MAC address (byte 1 in LSB) */
83: #define OPENETH_MAC_ADDR1_REG (OPENETH_BASE + 0x44)
84: 
85: /*  Location of the DMA descriptors */
86: #define OPENETH_DESC_BASE (OPENETH_BASE + 0x400)
87: /*  Total number of (TX + RX) DMA descriptors */
88: #define OPENETH_DESC_CNT 128
89: 
90: /****************************************************************************
91:  * Private Types
92:  ****************************************************************************/
93: 
94: struct openeth_priv_s
95: {
96:   struct netdev_lowerhalf_s dev;
97: 
98:   int cpuint; /* EMAC interrupt ID */
99: 
100:   int cur_rx_desc;
101:   int cur_tx_desc;
102:   uint8_t *rx_buf[RX_BUF_COUNT];
103:   uint8_t *tx_buf[TX_BUF_COUNT];
104: };
105: 
106: /*  Structures describing TX and RX descriptors. */
107: 
108: /*  The field names are same as in the OpenCores ethmac documentation. */
109: 
110: typedef struct
111: {
112:   uint16_t cs : 1;   /* !< Carrier sense lost (flag set by HW) */
113:   uint16_t df : 1;   /* !< Defer indication (flag set by HW) */
114:   uint16_t lc : 1;   /* !< Late collision occured (flag set by HW) */
115:   uint16_t rl : 1;   /* !< TX failed due to retransmission limit (flag set by HW) */
116:   uint16_t rtry : 4; /* !< Number of retries before the frame was sent (set by HW) */
117:   uint16_t ur : 1;   /* !< Underrun status (flag set by HW) */
118:   uint16_t rsv : 2;  /* !< Reserved */
119:   uint16_t crc : 1;  /* !< Add CRC at the end of the packet */
120:   uint16_t pad : 1;  /* !< Add padding to the end of short packets */
121:   uint16_t wr : 1;   /* !< Wrap-around. 0: not the last descriptor in the table, 1: last descriptor. */
122:   uint16_t irq : 1;  /* !< Generate interrupt after this descriptor is transmitted */
123:   uint16_t rd : 1;   /* !< Descriptor ready. 0: descriptor owned by SW, 1: descriptor owned by HW. Cleared by HW. */
124: 
125:   uint16_t len; /* !< Number of bytes to be transmitted */
126:   void *txpnt;  /* !< Pointer to the data to transmit */
127: } openeth_tx_desc_t;
128: 
129: static_assert(sizeof(openeth_tx_desc_t) == 8,
130:   "incorrect size of openeth_tx_desc_t");
131: 
132: typedef struct
133: {
134:   uint16_t lc : 1;  /* !< Late collision flag */
135:   uint16_t crc : 1; /* !< RX CRC error flag */
136:   uint16_t sf : 1;  /* !< Frame shorter than set in PACKETLEN register */
137:   uint16_t tl : 1;  /* !< Frame longer than set in PACKETLEN register */
138:   uint16_t dn : 1;  /* !< Dribble nibble (frame length not divisible by 8 bits) flag */
139:   uint16_t is : 1;  /* !< Invalid symbol flag */
140:   uint16_t or : 1;  /* !< Overrun flag */
141:   uint16_t m : 1;   /* !< Frame received because of the promiscuous mode */
142:   uint16_t rsv : 5; /* !< Reserved */
143:   uint16_t wr : 1;  /* !< Wrap-around. 0: not the last descriptor in the table, 1: last descriptor. */
144:   uint16_t irq : 1; /* !< Generate interrupt after this descriptor is transmitted */
145:   uint16_t e : 1;   /* !< The buffer is empty. 0: descriptor owned by SW, 1: descriptor owned by HW. */
146: 
147:   uint16_t len; /* !< Number of bytes received (filled by HW) */
148:   void *rxpnt;  /* !< Pointer to the receive buffer */
149: } openeth_rx_desc_t;
150: 
151: static_assert(sizeof(openeth_rx_desc_t) == 8,
152:   "incorrect size of openeth_rx_desc_t");

155:  * Private Function Prototypes
156:  ****************************************************************************/

158: /* NuttX callback functions */
159: 
160: static int openeth_ifup(struct netdev_lowerhalf_s *dev);
161: static int openeth_ifdown(struct netdev_lowerhalf_s *dev);
162: static int openeth_transmit(struct netdev_lowerhalf_s *dev, netpkt_t *pkt);

169: static struct openeth_priv_s g_openeth;
170: 
171: static const struct netdev_ops_s g_ops =
172: {
173:   .ifup     = openeth_ifup,
174:   .ifdown   = openeth_ifdown,
175:   .transmit = openeth_transmit,
176:   .receive  = openeth_receive,
177: };

183: static inline openeth_tx_desc_t *openeth_tx_desc(int idx)
184: {
185:   assert(idx < TX_BUF_COUNT);
186:   return &((openeth_tx_desc_t *)OPENETH_DESC_BASE)[idx];
187: }
188: 
189: static inline openeth_rx_desc_t *openeth_rx_desc(int idx)
190: {
191:   assert(idx < OPENETH_DESC_CNT - TX_BUF_COUNT);
192:   return &((openeth_rx_desc_t *)OPENETH_DESC_BASE)[idx + TX_BUF_COUNT];
193: }
194: 
195: static inline void openeth_enable(void)
196: {
197:   REG_SET_BIT(OPENETH_MODER_REG, OPENETH_TXEN | OPENETH_RXEN | OPENETH_PRO);
198:   REG_SET_BIT(OPENETH_INT_MASK_REG, OPENETH_INT_RXB);
199: }
200: 
201: static inline void openeth_disable(void)
202: {
203:   REG_CLR_BIT(OPENETH_INT_MASK_REG, OPENETH_INT_RXB);
204:   REG_CLR_BIT(OPENETH_MODER_REG, OPENETH_TXEN | OPENETH_RXEN | OPENETH_PRO);
205: }
206: 
207: static inline void openeth_reset(void)
208: {
209:   REG_SET_BIT(OPENETH_MODER_REG, OPENETH_RST);
210:   REG_CLR_BIT(OPENETH_MODER_REG, OPENETH_RST);
211: }
212: 
213: static inline void openeth_init_tx_desc(openeth_tx_desc_t *desc, void *buf)
214: {
215:   *desc = (openeth_tx_desc_t)
216:     {
217:       .rd = 0,
218:       .txpnt = buf,
219:     };
220: }
221: 
222: static inline void openeth_init_rx_desc(openeth_rx_desc_t *desc, void *buf)
223: {
224:   *desc = (openeth_rx_desc_t)
225:     {
226:       .e = 1,
227:       .irq = 1,
228:       .rxpnt = buf,
229:     };
230: }
231: 
232: static inline void openeth_set_tx_desc_cnt(int tx_desc_cnt)
233: {
234:   assert(tx_desc_cnt <= OPENETH_DESC_CNT);
235:   REG_WRITE(OPENETH_TX_BD_NUM_REG, tx_desc_cnt);
236: }
237: 
238: static IRAM_ATTR int openeth_isr_handler(int irq, void *context, void *arg)
239: {
240:   struct netdev_lowerhalf_s *dev = &g_openeth.dev;
241: 
242:   uint32_t status = REG_READ(OPENETH_INT_SOURCE_REG);
243: 
244:   if (status & OPENETH_INT_RXB)
245:     {
246:       netdev_lower_rxready(dev);
247:     }
248: 
249:   if (status & OPENETH_INT_BUSY)
250:     {
251:       ninfo("RX frame dropped (0x%x)", status);
252:     }
253: 
254:   /* Clear interrupt */
255: 
256:   REG_WRITE(OPENETH_INT_SOURCE_REG, status);
257: 
258:   return 0;
259: }
260: 
261: static netpkt_t *openeth_receive(struct netdev_lowerhalf_s *dev)
262: {
263:   netpkt_t *pkt = netpkt_alloc(dev, NETPKT_RX);
264: 
265:   struct openeth_priv_s *priv = &g_openeth;
266: 
267:   if (pkt)
268:     {
269:       openeth_rx_desc_t *desc_ptr = openeth_rx_desc(priv->cur_rx_desc);
270:       openeth_rx_desc_t desc_val = *desc_ptr;
271: 
272:       ninfo("desc %d (%p) e=%d len=%d wr=%d",
273:         priv->cur_rx_desc, desc_ptr, desc_val.e, desc_val.len, desc_val.wr);
274: 
275:       if (desc_val.e)
276:         {
277:           ninfo("descriptor is not owned by HW (e=%d)", desc_val.e);
278:           goto err;
279:         }
280: 
281:       if (!desc_val.len)
282:         {
283:           nerr("ERROR desc_val.len is zero");
284:           goto err;
285:         }
286: 
287:       netpkt_copyin(dev, pkt, desc_val.rxpnt, desc_val.len, 0);
288: 
289:       /* Free up the descriptor */
290: 
291:       desc_val.e = 1;
292:       desc_val.len = 0;
293:       *desc_ptr = desc_val;
294: 
295:       priv->cur_rx_desc = (priv->cur_rx_desc + 1) % RX_BUF_COUNT;
296:     }
297: 
298:   return pkt;
299: 
300: err:
301:   netpkt_free(dev, pkt, NETPKT_RX);
302:   return NULL;
303: }

305: /****************************************************************************
306:  * Name: openeth_ifup
307:  *
308:  * Description:
309:  *   NuttX Callback: Bring up the Ethernet interface when an IP address is
310:  *   provided
311:  *
312:  * Input Parameters:
313:  *   dev - Reference to the NuttX driver state structure
314:  *
315:  * Returned Value:
316:  *   None
317:  *
318:  * Assumptions:
319:  *
320:  ****************************************************************************/
321: 
322: static int openeth_ifup(struct netdev_lowerhalf_s *dev)
323: {
324:   irqstate_t flags;
325: 
326:   /* Disable the Ethernet interrupt */
327: 
328:   flags = enter_critical_section();
329: 
330:   /* Enable TX and RX */
331: 
332:   openeth_enable();
333: 
334:   leave_critical_section(flags);
335: 
336:   netdev_lower_carrier_on(dev);
337: 
338:   return OK;
339: }
340: 
341: /****************************************************************************
342:  * Name: openeth_ifdown
343:  *
344:  * Description:
345:  *   NuttX Callback: Stop the interface.
346:  *
347:  * Input Parameters:
348:  *   dev - Reference to the NuttX driver state structure
349:  *
350:  * Returned Value:
351:  *   None
352:  *
353:  * Assumptions:
354:  *
355:  ****************************************************************************/
356: 
357: static int openeth_ifdown(struct netdev_lowerhalf_s *dev)
358: {
359:   irqstate_t flags;
360: 
361:   /* Disable the Ethernet interrupt */
362: 
363:   flags = enter_critical_section();
364: 
365:   /* Disable TX and RX */
366: 
367:   openeth_enable();
368: 
369:   leave_critical_section(flags);
370: 
371:   netdev_lower_carrier_off(dev);
372: 
373:   return OK;
374: }
375: 
376: static int openeth_transmit(struct netdev_lowerhalf_s *dev,
377:                             netpkt_t *pkt)
378: {
379:   struct openeth_priv_s *priv = (struct openeth_priv_s *)dev;
380:   unsigned int len = netpkt_getdatalen(dev, pkt);
381: 
382:   /*  In QEMU, there never is a TX operation in progress */
383: 
384:   /* Copyout the L2 data and transmit. */
385: 
386:   netpkt_copyout(dev, priv->tx_buf[priv->cur_tx_desc], pkt, len, 0);
387: 
388:   /* Do Transmit */
389: 
390:   openeth_tx_desc_t *desc_ptr = openeth_tx_desc(priv->cur_tx_desc);
391:   openeth_tx_desc_t desc_val = *desc_ptr;
392: 
393:   desc_val.wr = (priv->cur_tx_desc == TX_BUF_COUNT - 1);
394:   desc_val.len = len;
395:   desc_val.rd = 1;
396:   *desc_ptr = desc_val;
397: 
398:   /* Free the buffer and notify the upper layer */
399: 
400:   netpkt_free(dev, pkt, NETPKT_TX);
401:   netdev_lower_txdone(dev);
402: 
403:   return OK;
404: }
