406: static int openeth_set_addr(uint8_t *addr)
407: {
408:   ninfo("set mac\n");
409:   if (!addr)
410:     {
411:       nerr("can't set mac addr to null");
412:       goto err;
413:     }
414: 
415:   const uint8_t mac0[4] = {
416:     addr[5], addr[4], addr[3], addr[2]
417:   };
418: 
419:   const uint8_t mac1[4] = {
420:     addr[1], addr[0]
421:   };
422: 
423:   uint32_t mac0_u32;
424:   uint32_t mac1_u32;
425:   memcpy(&mac0_u32, &mac0, 4);
426:   memcpy(&mac1_u32, &mac1, 4);
427:   REG_WRITE(OPENETH_MAC_ADDR0_REG, mac0_u32);
428:   REG_WRITE(OPENETH_MAC_ADDR1_REG, mac1_u32);
429:   return 0;
430: err:
431:   return -1;
432: }

434: /****************************************************************************
435:  * Public Functions
436:  ****************************************************************************/
437: 
438: /****************************************************************************
439:  * Name: esp_openeth_initialize
440:  *
441:  * Description:
442:  *   Initialize the openeth driver
443:  *
444:  * Input Parameters:
445:  *   None
446:  *
447:  * Returned Value:
448:  *   OK on success; Negated errno on failure.
449:  *
450:  ****************************************************************************/
451: 
452: int esp_openeth_initialize(void)
453: {
454:   int ret;
455:   struct openeth_priv_s *priv = &g_openeth;
456:   struct netdev_lowerhalf_s *dev = &priv->dev;
457: 
458:   /* Sanity check */
459: 
460:   if (REG_READ(OPENETH_MODER_REG) != OPENETH_MODER_DEFAULT)
461:     {
462:       nerr("Openeth should only be used when running in QEMU.");
463:       nerr("When running the app on the real hardware,"
464:            "use the real MAC instead.");
465:       abort();
466:     }
467: 
468:   /* Initialize the driver structure */
469: 
470:   memset(priv, 0, sizeof(struct openeth_priv_s));
471: 
472:   dev->ops = &g_ops;
473: 
474:   dev->quota[NETPKT_TX] = TX_BUF_COUNT;
475:   dev->quota[NETPKT_RX] = RX_BUF_COUNT;
476: 
477:   /* Allocate DMA buffers */
478: 
479:   for (int i = 0; i < RX_BUF_COUNT; i++)
480:     {
481:       priv->rx_buf[i] = kmm_calloc(1, DMA_BUF_SIZE);
482:       if (!(priv->rx_buf[i]))
483:         {
484:           nerr("ERROR: Failed allocate RX descriptors\n");
485:           ret = -ENOMEM;
486:           goto err;
487:         }
488: 
489:       openeth_init_rx_desc(openeth_rx_desc(i), priv->rx_buf[i]);
490:     }
491: 
492:   openeth_rx_desc(RX_BUF_COUNT - 1)->wr = 1;
493:   priv->cur_rx_desc = 0;
494: 
495:   for (int i = 0; i < TX_BUF_COUNT; i++)
496:     {
497:       priv->tx_buf[i] = kmm_calloc(1, DMA_BUF_SIZE);
498:       if (!(priv->tx_buf[i]))
499:         {
500:           nerr("ERROR: Failed allocate TX descriptors\n");
501:           ret = -ENOMEM;
502:           goto err;
503:         }
504: 
505:       openeth_init_tx_desc(openeth_tx_desc(i), priv->tx_buf[i]);
506:     }
507: 
508:   openeth_tx_desc(TX_BUF_COUNT - 1)->wr = 1;
509:   priv->cur_tx_desc = 0;
510: 
511:   /* Setup interrupts */
512: 
513:   priv->cpuint = OPENETH_SETUP_IRQ(0, OPENETH_PERIPH_MAC,
514:                                  1, OPENETH_CPUINT_LEVEL);
515:   if (priv->cpuint < 0)
516:     {
517:       nerr("ERROR: Failed allocate interrupt\n");
518:       ret = -ENOMEM;
519:       goto err;
520:     }
521: 
522:   /* Initialize the MAC */
523: 
524:   openeth_reset();
525:   openeth_set_tx_desc_cnt(TX_BUF_COUNT);
526:   memcpy(priv->dev.netdev.d_mac.ether.ether_addr_octet,
527:     "\x00\x02\x03\x04\x05\x06\x07\x08", ETH_ALEN);
528:   openeth_set_addr(priv->dev.netdev.d_mac.ether.ether_addr_octet);
529: 
530:   /* Attach the interrupt */
531: 
532:   ret = irq_attach(OPENETH_IRQ_MAC, openeth_isr_handler, priv);
533: 
534:   /* Register the device with the OS so that socket IOCTLs can be
535:    * performed.
536:    */
537: 
538:   ret = netdev_lower_register(dev, NET_LL_ETHERNET);
539:   if (ret)
540:     {
541:       nerr("ERROR: netdev_lower_register\n");
542:       goto err;
543:     }
544: 
545:   /* Put the network in the UP state */
546: 
547:   return openeth_ifup(dev);
548: 
549: err:
550:   nerr("Failed initializing ret = %d", ret);
551:   abort();
552: }

693: /****************************************************************************
694:  * Function: netdev_upper_rxpoll_work
695:  *
696:  * Description:
697:  *   Try to receive packets from device and pass packets into IP
698:  *   stack and send packets which is from IP stack if necessary.
699:  *
700:  * Input Parameters:
701:  *   upper - Reference to the upper half driver structure
702:  *
703:  * Assumptions:
704:  *   Called with the network locked.
705:  *
706:  ****************************************************************************/
707: 
708: static void netdev_upper_rxpoll_work(FAR struct netdev_upperhalf_s *upper)
709: {
710:   FAR struct netdev_lowerhalf_s *lower = upper->lower;
711:   FAR struct net_driver_s       *dev   = &lower->netdev;
712:   FAR netpkt_t                  *pkt;
713: 
714:   /* Loop while receive() successfully retrieves valid Ethernet frames. */
715: 
716:   netdev_lock(dev);
717:   while ((pkt = lower->ops->receive(lower)) != NULL)
718:     {
719:       if (!IFF_IS_UP(dev->d_flags))
720:         {
721:           /* Interface down, drop frame */
722: 
723:           NETDEV_RXDROPPED(dev);
724:           netpkt_free(lower, pkt, NETPKT_RX);
725:           nerr("ERROR: Dropped frame due to lower dev not up\n");
726:           continue;
727:         }
728: 
729:       netpkt_put(dev, pkt, NETPKT_RX);
730:       NETDEV_RXPACKETS(dev);
731: 
732: #ifdef CONFIG_NET_PKT
733:       /* When packet sockets are enabled, feed the frame into the tap */
734: 
735:       pkt_input(dev);
736: #endif
737: 
738:       switch (dev->d_lltype)
739:         {
740: #ifdef CONFIG_NET_LOOPBACK
741:         case NET_LL_LOOPBACK:
742: #endif
743: #ifdef CONFIG_NET_ETHERNET
744:         case NET_LL_ETHERNET:
745: #endif
746: #ifdef CONFIG_DRIVERS_IEEE80211
747:         case NET_LL_IEEE80211:
748: #endif
749: #if defined(CONFIG_NET_LOOPBACK) || defined(CONFIG_NET_ETHERNET) || \
750:     defined(CONFIG_DRIVERS_IEEE80211)
751:           eth_input(dev);
752:           break;
753: #endif
754: #ifdef CONFIG_NET_MBIM
755:         case NET_LL_MBIM:
756:           ip_input(dev);
757:           break;
758: #endif
759: #ifdef CONFIG_NET_CAN
760:         case NET_LL_CAN:
761:           ninfo("CAN frame");
762:           can_input(dev);
763:           break;
764: #endif
765:         default:
766:           nerr("Unknown link type %d\n", dev->d_lltype);
767:           break;
768:         }
769:     }
770: 
771:   netdev_unlock(dev);
772: }

790:   netdev_upper_vlan_foreach(upper, netdev_lower_txdone);

799: /****************************************************************************
800:  * Name: netdev_upper_loop
801:  *
802:  * Description:
803:  *   The loop for dedicated thread.
804:  *
805:  ****************************************************************************/
806: 
807: static int netdev_upper_loop(int argc, FAR char *argv[])
808: {
809:   FAR struct netdev_upperhalf_s *upper =
810:     (FAR struct netdev_upperhalf_s *)((uintptr_t)strtoul(argv[1], NULL, 16));
811:   int cpu = atoi(argv[2]);
812:   FAR struct netdev_thread_s *t = &upper->thread[cpu];
813: 
814:   if (upper->lower->rxtype == NETDEV_RX_THREAD_RSS)
815:     {
816:       cpu_set_t cpuset;
817: 
818:       CPU_ZERO(&cpuset);
819:       CPU_SET(cpu, &cpuset);
820:       sched_setaffinity(t->tid, sizeof(cpu_set_t), &cpuset);
821:     }
822: 
823:   while (nxsem_wait(&t->sem) == OK && t->tid != INVALID_PROCESS_ID)
824:     {
825:       netdev_upper_work(upper);
826:     }
827: 
828:   nwarn("WARNING: Netdev work thread quitting.");
829:   nxsem_post(&t->sem_exit);
830:   return 0;
831: }

833: /****************************************************************************
834:  * Name: netdev_upper_queue_work
835:  *
836:  * Description:
837:  *   Called when there is any work to do.
838:  *
839:  * Input Parameters:
840:  *   dev - Reference to the NuttX driver state structure
841:  *
842:  ****************************************************************************/
843: 
844: static inline void netdev_upper_queue_work(FAR struct net_driver_s *dev)
845: {
846:   FAR struct netdev_upperhalf_s *upper = dev->d_private;
847:   int cpu = 0;
848: 
849:   switch (upper->lower->rxtype)
850:     {
851:       case NETDEV_RX_WORK:
852:         {
853:           FAR struct work_s *work = upper->work;
854:           if (work_available(work))
855:             {
856:               /* Schedule to serialize the poll on the worker thread. */
857: 
858:               work_queue(upper->lower->priority, work, netdev_upper_work,
859:                          upper, 0);
860:             }
861:         }
862:         break;
863:       case NETDEV_RX_THREAD_RSS:
864:         cpu = this_cpu();
865:       case NETDEV_RX_THREAD:
866:         {
867:           FAR struct netdev_thread_s *t = &upper->thread[cpu];
868:           int semcount;
869: 
870:           if (nxsem_get_value(&t->sem, &semcount) == OK && semcount <= 0)
871:             {
872:               nxsem_post(&t->sem);
873:             }
874:         }
875:         break;
876:     }
877: }

168:  *               EVENT_WIFI_STA_DISCONNECTED event, it's user app's responsibility to

267:  *    scan done event callback.

270:  * Usage example:
271:  *
272:  *     //Define your scan done handler
273:  *     int scan_done_handler(void *arg, event_module_t event_module, int event_id, void *event_data)
274:  *     {
275:  *         wifi_scan_result_t scan_result = {0};
276:  *
277:  *         BK_LOG_ON_ERR(bk_wifi_scan_get_result(&scan_result));
278:  *         bk_wifi_scan_dump_result(&scan_result);
279:  *         bk_wifi_scan_free_result(&scan_result);
280:  *
281:  *         return BK_OK;
282:  *     }
283:  *
284:  *     //Start the scan
285:  *     wifi_scan_config_t config = {0};

287:  *     BK_LOG_ON_ERR(bk_event_register_cb(EVENT_MOD_WIFI, EVENT_WIFI_SCAN_DONE, scan_done_handler, NULL));

292:  * @attention 3. Make sure the reserved fields in scan_config is zero, otherwise you may

297:  *
298:  * @return
299:  *    - BK_OK: succeed

757: /**
758:  * @brief     Set the filter configuration
759:  *
760:  * The filter is used to configure what kind of management packets can be received
761:  * by the filter callback registered by bk_wifi_filter_register_cb().
762:  *
763:  * Per the WiFi receiving data path, the management frames are firstly received by
764:  * WiFi hardware, then the hardware relays them to WiFi software (WiFi driver). Normally
765:  * the hardware receives all management frames in the air, however it don't
766:  * relay all of them to WiFi driver (WiFi software), it only relays management frames
767:  * necessary to STA or AP or scan or monitor, depends on which interface or function are
768:  * enabled. In other word, WiFi driver only receives management frames necessary to them
769:  * from hardware.
770:  *
771:  * When no filter callback is registered, all management frame processing is ended
772:  * in WiFi driver unless the filter callback is registered.
773:  *
774:  * If filter callback is register and if filter_config.rx_all_default_mgmt is set to 1,
775:  * then all the management frames received by WiFi driver are relayed to the filter
776:  * callback. **Notified that the default management frame types can be received depends
777:  * on whether STA or AP or scan or monitor are enabled or not, e.g. when only STA is
778:  * enabled, the WiFi driver needs to handle PROBE response, but don't need to handle PROBE
779:  * request, so the WiFi driver only receive PROBE response from WiFi hardware**.
780:  *
781:  * Here is summary about default management frame received by WiFi:
782:  *  Condition      | Default management frame
783:  * ----------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------
784:  *  STA connected  | Management frames sent by the connected AP, such as beacon etc.
785:  *  AP started     | Management frames sent by connected STA and probe request etc.
786:  *  Scan starting  | Probe response and beacon frames of all APs.
787:  *  Monitor started| All kind of management frames
788:  *
789:  * How about if the filter callback wants to receive more management frame types,
790:  * e.g. want to receive PROBE request when only STA is enabled. We can set
791:  * filter_config->rx_probe_req to receive PROBE response no matter whether AP is enabled
792:  * or NOT.
793:  *
794:  * Usage example:
795:  *
796:  *     // Only receive management frame default received by WiFi driver
797:  *     // Equal to the case when bk_wifi_filter_set_config() is not called
798:  *     wifi_filter_config_t filter_config = WIFI_DEFAULT_FILTER_CONFIG();
799:  *     BK_LOG_ON_ERR(bk_wifi_filter_set_config(&filter_config);
800:  *
801:  *     // Receive all beacon and management frames default received by WiFi driver
802:  *     filter_config.rx_all_beacon = 1;
803:  *     BK_LOG_ON_ERR(bk_wifi_filter_set_config(&filter_config);
804:  *
805:  *     // Only receive all beacon
806:  *     filter_config.rx_all_beacon = 1;
807:  *     filter_config.rx_all_default_mgmt = 0;
808:  *     BK_LOG_ON_ERR(bk_wifi_filter_set_config(&filter_config);
809:  *
810:  * @attention 1. If this API is not called, the default filter is to relay all
811:  *               mamangement frames received by WiFi driver to the filter callback.
812:  * @attention 2. If STA is enabled, the WiFi driver only receives beacon from the
813:  *               connected AP, if scan is enabled or filter_config->rx_all_beacon
814:  *               is set, the WiFi driver receives beacons of all APs.
815:  *
816:  * @param filter_config configuration of filter
817:  *
818:  * @return
819:  *    - BK_OK: succeed
820:  *    - others: other errors
821:  */
822: bk_err_t bk_wifi_filter_set_config(const wifi_filter_config_t *filter_config);
823: 
824: /**
825:  * @brief     Get the filter configuration
826:  *
827:  * @param filter_config store configuration of filter
828:  *
829:  * @return
830:  *    - BK_OK: succeed
831:  *    - others: other errors
832:  */
833: bk_err_t bk_wifi_filter_get_config(wifi_filter_config_t *filter_config);
834: 
835: /**
836:  * @brief     Register the filter user callback
837:  *
838:  * @attention 1. If the monitor is enabled, the management packets received by filter
839:  *               callback can also be received by monitor callback. If this is not what
840:  *               we want, we can disable filter when enabling monitor, or disable monitor
841:  *               when enabling filter.
842:  * @attention 2. During WiFi scan, the filter also works.
843:  * @attention 3. Pass NULL callback or set all fields of filter_config to 0 to disable the
844:  *               filter.
845:  * @attention 4. The memory used to hold the frame buffer and frame_info will be freed
846:  *               immediately when the callback is returned, so don't relay them to other
847:  *               task. Make a copy of them and then relay to other task if necessary.

849:  *               WiFi driver core thread, otherwise it may impact the WiFi performance.
850:  *
851:  * @param filter_cb the filter user callback
852:  *
853:  * @return
854:  *    - BK_OK: succeed

856:  */

106: 		the MSS (Maximum Segment Size).  SLIP has no link layer header so for
107: 		SLIP the MTU is the same as the PKTSIZE.
108: 
109: 		SLIP is required to support at least 256+20+20 = 296.  Values other than
110: 		296 are not recommended.
111: 
112: 		The Linux slip module hard-codes its MTU size to 296 (40 bytes for
113: 		the IP+TCP headers plus 256 bytes of data).  So you might as well

120: 		256 MSS, but restrict transfers to 128 bytes (possibly by modifying
121: 		the MSS value in the TCP connection structure).

21: 	default 8 if !NET_WRITE_BUFFERS && !NET_READAHEAD
22: 	---help---
23: 		Each packet is represented by a series of small I/O buffers in a

25: 		buffers available for packet data.

27: config IOB_BUFSIZE

33: 		Each packet is represented by a series of small I/O buffers in a

35: 		I/O buffer.
36: 
37: config IOB_ALIGNMENT
38: 	int "Alignment size of each I/O buffer"

45: 	string "The section where iob buffer is located"
46: 	---help---

51: 	int "Number of pre-allocated I/O buffer chain heads"
52: 	default 0 if !NET_READAHEAD
53: 	default IOB_NBUFFERS if NET_READAHEAD
54: 	---help---
55: 		These tiny nodes are used as "containers" to support queueing of
56: 		I/O buffer chains.  This will limit the number of I/O transactions
57: 		that can be "in-flight" at any give time.  The default value of
58: 		zero disables this features.
59: 
60: 		These generic I/O buffer chain containers are not currently used
61: 		by any logic in NuttX.  That is because their other specialized
62: 		I/O buffer chain containers that also carry a payload of usage
63: 		specific information.
64: 
65: 		Note: TCP and UDP don't use this.
66: 		Note: ICMP/ICMPv6 and CAN use this.
67: 
68: config IOB_THROTTLE
69: 	int "I/O buffer throttle value"
70: 	default 0 if !NET_WRITE_BUFFERS || !NET_READAHEAD
71: 	default 8 if NET_WRITE_BUFFERS && NET_READAHEAD
72: 	---help---
73: 		TCP write buffering and read-ahead buffer use the same pool of free
74: 		I/O buffers.  In order to prevent uncontrolled incoming TCP packets
75: 		from hogging all of the available, pre-allocated I/O buffers, a
76: 		throttling value is required.  This throttle value assures that

78: 		are halted.

87: 		function on the high priority work queue when an IOB is available.

97: 	---help---
98: 		IOBs may become available at very high rates and the resulting
99: 		notification processing can be substantial even if there is nothing
100: 		waiting for a free IOB.  This divider will reduce that rate of

670: static FAR struct wifi_sim_bss_s *select_bss(FAR struct wifi_sim_s *sta,
671:                                              FAR char *bss_buf)
672: {
673:   char bss[256];
674:   FAR char *s;
675:   FAR char *p;
676:   struct wifi_sim_bss_s bss_info;
677:   FAR struct wifi_sim_bss_s *sbss = NULL;
678:   bool bss_found = false;
679: 
680:   for (p = bss_buf; *p != '\0'; p++)
681:     {
682:       s = p;
683:       while (*p != '\n')
684:         {
685:           p++;
686:         }
687: 
688:       memset(bss, 0, sizeof(bss));
689:       memcpy(bss, s, p - s + 1);
690:       wifidriver_get_bssinfo(&bss_info, bss, strlen(bss));
691: 
692:       /* compare bssid or essid, and security */
693: 
694:       if ((sta->ssid_flag == 2 && !memcmp(sta->bssid, bss_info.bssid, 6)) ||
695:           (sta->ssid_flag == 1 && !memcmp(sta->ssid, bss_info.ssid, 32)))
696:         {
697:           /* cmp security */
698: 
699:           if (sta->psk_flag == 0)
700:             {
701:               if (!strstr(bss_info.security, "WPA") &&
702:                   !strstr(bss_info.security, "WEP"))
703:                 {
704:                   bss_found = true;
705:                 }
706:               else
707:                 {
708:                   nerr("security doesn't match");
709:                 }
710: 
711:               break;
712:             }
713:           else if (get_cipherstr(sta->pairwise_chiper) &&
714:                    strstr(bss_info.security,
715:                           get_cipherstr(sta->pairwise_chiper)))
716:             {
717:               bss_found = true;
718:               break;
719:             }
720:           else
721:             {
722:               nerr("security doesn't match");
723:             }
724:         }
725:     }
726: 
727:   if (bss_found)
728:     {
729:       sbss = malloc(sizeof(struct wifi_sim_bss_s));
730:       if (sbss == NULL)
731:         {
732:           nerr("select bss  malloc failed!");
733:           return NULL;
734:         }
735: 
736:       memcpy(sbss, &bss_info, sizeof(struct wifi_sim_bss_s));
737:     }
738:   else
739:     {
740:       nerr("No BSS match.");
741:     }
742: 
743:   return sbss;
744: }

262:  * Name: netdev_register
263:  *
264:  * Description:
265:  *   Register a network device driver and assign a name to it so that it can
266:  *   be found in subsequent network ioctl operations on the device.
267:  *
268:  *   A custom, device-specific interface name format string may be selected
269:  *   by putting that format string into the device structure's d_ifname[]
270:  *   array before calling netdev_register().  Otherwise, the d_ifname[] must
271:  *   be zeroed on entry.
272:  *
273:  * Input Parameters:
274:  *   dev    - The device driver structure to be registered.
275:  *   lltype - Link level protocol used by the driver (Ethernet, SLIP, TUN,
276:  *            ...)
277:  *
278:  * Returned Value:
279:  *   0:Success; negated errno on failure
280:  *
281:  * Assumptions:
282:  *   Called during system bring-up, but also when a removable network
283:  *   device is installed.
284:  *
285:  ****************************************************************************/
286: 
287: int netdev_register(FAR struct net_driver_s *dev, enum net_lltype_e lltype)
288: {
289:   FAR struct net_driver_s **last;
290:   FAR char devfmt_str[IFNAMSIZ];
291:   FAR const char *devfmt;
292:   uint32_t flags   = 0;
293:   uint16_t pktsize = 0;
294:   uint8_t llhdrlen = 0;
295:   int devnum;
296: #ifdef CONFIG_NETDEV_IFINDEX
297:   int ifindex;
298: #endif
299: 
300:   if (dev != NULL)
301:     {
302:       /* Set the protocol used by the device and the size of the link
303:        * header used by this protocol.
304:        */
305: 
306:       switch (lltype)
307:         {
308: #ifdef CONFIG_NET_LOOPBACK
309:           case NET_LL_LOOPBACK:   /* Local loopback */
310:             llhdrlen = 0;
311:             pktsize  = NET_LO_PKTSIZE;
312:             devfmt   = NETDEV_LO_FORMAT;
313:             flags    = IFF_LOOPBACK;
314:             break;
315: #endif
316: 
317: #ifdef CONFIG_NET_ETHERNET
318:           case NET_LL_ETHERNET:   /* Ethernet */
319:             llhdrlen = ETH_HDRLEN;
320:             pktsize  = CONFIG_NET_ETH_PKTSIZE;
321:             devfmt   = NETDEV_ETH_FORMAT;
322:             flags    = IFF_BROADCAST | IFF_MULTICAST;
323:             break;
324: #endif
325: 
326: #ifdef CONFIG_DRIVERS_IEEE80211
327:           case NET_LL_IEEE80211:  /* IEEE 802.11 */
328:             llhdrlen = ETH_HDRLEN;
329:             pktsize  = CONFIG_NET_ETH_PKTSIZE;
330:             devfmt   = NETDEV_WLAN_FORMAT;
331:             flags    = IFF_BROADCAST | IFF_MULTICAST;
332:             break;
333: #endif
334: 
335: #ifdef CONFIG_NET_CAN
336:           case NET_LL_CAN:  /* CAN bus */
337:             dev->d_llhdrlen = 0;
338:             dev->d_pktsize  = NET_CAN_PKTSIZE;
339:             devfmt          = NETDEV_CAN_FORMAT;
340:             flags           = IFF_NOARP;
341:             break;
342: #endif
343: 
344: #ifdef CONFIG_NET_BLUETOOTH
345:           case NET_LL_BLUETOOTH:              /* Bluetooth */
346:             llhdrlen = BLUETOOTH_MAX_HDRLEN;  /* Determined at runtime */
347: #ifdef CONFIG_NET_6LOWPAN
348:             pktsize  = CONFIG_NET_6LOWPAN_PKTSIZE;
349: #endif
350:             devfmt   = NETDEV_BNEP_FORMAT;
351:             flags    = IFF_BROADCAST | IFF_MULTICAST;
352:             break;
353: #endif
354: 
355: #if defined(CONFIG_NET_6LOWPAN) || defined(CONFIG_NET_IEEE802154)
356:           case NET_LL_IEEE802154: /* IEEE 802.15.4 MAC */
357:           case NET_LL_PKTRADIO:   /* Non-IEEE 802.15.4 packet radio */
358:             llhdrlen = 0;         /* Determined at runtime */
359: #ifdef CONFIG_NET_6LOWPAN
360:             pktsize  = CONFIG_NET_6LOWPAN_PKTSIZE;
361: #endif
362:             devfmt   = NETDEV_WPAN_FORMAT;
363:             flags    = IFF_POINTOPOINT | IFF_NOARP | IFF_MULTICAST;
364:             break;
365: #endif
366: 
367: #ifdef CONFIG_NET_SLIP
368:           case NET_LL_SLIP:       /* Serial Line Internet Protocol (SLIP) */
369:             llhdrlen = 0;
370:             pktsize  = CONFIG_NET_SLIP_PKTSIZE;
371:             devfmt   = NETDEV_SLIP_FORMAT;
372:             flags    = IFF_POINTOPOINT | IFF_NOARP | IFF_MULTICAST;
373:             break;
374: #endif
375: 
376: #ifdef CONFIG_NET_TUN
377:           case NET_LL_TUN:        /* Virtual Network Device (TUN) */
378:             llhdrlen = 0;         /* This will be overwritten by tun_ioctl
379:                                    * if used as a TAP (layer 2) device */
380:             pktsize  = CONFIG_NET_TUN_PKTSIZE;
381:             devfmt   = NETDEV_TUN_FORMAT;
382:             flags    = IFF_POINTOPOINT | IFF_NOARP | IFF_MULTICAST;
383:             break;
384: #endif
385: 
386: #ifdef CONFIG_NET_MBIM
387:           case NET_LL_MBIM:
388:             llhdrlen = 0;
389:             pktsize  = 1200;
390:             devfmt   = NETDEV_WWAN_FORMAT;
391:             flags    = IFF_BROADCAST | IFF_NOARP | IFF_MULTICAST;
392:             break;
393: #endif
394: 
395: #ifdef CONFIG_NET_CELLULAR
396:           case NET_LL_CELL:
397:             llhdrlen = 0;
398:             pktsize  = CONFIG_NET_ETH_PKTSIZE;
399:             devfmt   = NETDEV_CELL_FORMAT;
400:             flags    = IFF_NOARP;
401:             break;
402: #endif
403: 
404:           default:
405:             nerr("ERROR: Unrecognized link type: %d\n", lltype);
406:             return -EINVAL;
407:         }
408: 
409:       /* Update the package length.  A network driver may provide custom
410:        * values for MAC header length and for the maximum packet size.  Some
411:        * driver implementations (for example, the simulator) will require
412:        * dynamic MTU calculations to support tunneling (as an example).
413:        */

415:       if (dev->d_llhdrlen == 0)

418:         }

423:         }

431:       /* There are no clients of the device yet */
432: 
433:       dev->d_conncb = NULL;
434:       dev->d_conncb_tail = NULL;
435:       dev->d_devcb = NULL;

49:  *   is required for some drivers but, if there are not complaints,
50:  *   can be safely disabled.  The worker thread also performs
51:  *   from interrupt handlers.  If the worker thread is disabled,
52:  *   then that clean will be performed by the IDLE thread instead
53:  *   (which runs at the lowest of priority and may not be appropriate
54:  *   if memory reclamation is of high priority).  If CONFIG_SCHED_HPWORK
55:  *   is enabled, then the following options can also be used:
56:  * CONFIG_SCHED_HPNTHREADS - The number of thread in the high-priority
57:  *   queue's thread pool.  Default: 1
58:  * CONFIG_SCHED_HPWORKPRIORITY - The execution priority of the high-
59:  *   priority worker thread.  Default: 224

64:  *   priority work queue will be created.  This lower priority work queue

162: /****************************************************************************
163:  * Name: wapi_freq2float
164:  *
165:  * Description:
166:  *   Converts internal representation of frequencies to a floating point.
167:  *
168:  ****************************************************************************/
169: 
170: static inline double wapi_freq2float(const struct iw_freq *freq)
171: {
172:   return ((double)freq->m) * pow(10, freq->e);
173: }

175: /****************************************************************************
176:  * Name: wapi_float2freq
177:  *
178:  * Description:
179:  *   Converts a floating point the our internal representation of
180:  *   frequencies.
181:  *
182:  ****************************************************************************/
183: 
184: static inline void wapi_float2freq(double floatfreq, struct iw_freq *freq)
185: {
186:   freq->e = (short)floor(log10(floatfreq));
187:   if (freq->e > 8)
188:     {
189:       freq->m = ((long)(floor(floatfreq / pow(10, freq->e - 6)))) * 100;
190:       freq->e -= 8;
191:     }
192:   else
193:     {
194:       freq->m = (long)floatfreq;
195:       freq->e = 0;
196:     }
197: }

259:  * Description:
260:  *   Extract the next event from the stream.
261:  *
262:  ****************************************************************************/

264: static int wapi_event_stream_extract(FAR struct wapi_event_stream_s *stream,
265:                                      FAR struct iw_event *iwe)
266: {
267:   int ret = 1;
268:   FAR struct iw_event *iwe_stream;
269: 
270:   iwe_stream = (FAR struct iw_event *)stream->current;
271: 
272:   if (stream->current + offsetof(struct iw_event, u) > stream->end ||
273:       iwe_stream->len == 0)
274:     {
275:       /* Nothing to process */
276: 
277:       return 0;
278:     }
279: 
280:   if (stream->current + iwe_stream->len > stream->end ||
281:       iwe_stream->len < offsetof(struct iw_event, u))
282:     {
283:       return -EINVAL;
284:     }
285: 
286:   switch (iwe_stream->cmd)
287:     {
288:       case SIOCGIWESSID:
289:       case SIOCGIWENCODE:
290:       case IWEVGENIE:
291:         iwe->cmd = iwe_stream->cmd;
292:         iwe->len = offsetof(struct iw_event, u) + sizeof(struct iw_point);
293:         iwe->u.data.flags = iwe_stream->u.data.flags;
294:         iwe->u.data.length = iwe_stream->u.data.length;
295: 
296:         iwe->u.data.pointer = (FAR void *)(stream->current +
297:                               offsetof(struct iw_event, u) +
298:                               (unsigned long)iwe_stream->u.data.pointer);
299:         break;
300: 
301:       default:
302:         if (iwe_stream->len > sizeof(*iwe))
303:           {
304:             WAPI_ERROR("Unhandled event size 0x%x %d\n", iwe_stream->cmd,
305:                                                          iwe_stream->len);
306:             iwe->cmd = 0;
307:             iwe->len = offsetof(struct iw_event, u);
308:             break;
309:           }
310: 
311:         memcpy(iwe, iwe_stream, iwe_stream->len);
312:     }
313: 
314:   /* Update stream to next event */
315: 
316:   stream->current += iwe_stream->len;
317:   return ret;
318: }

322:  *
323:  * Description:
324:  *

327: static int wapi_scan_event(FAR struct iw_event *event,
328:                            FAR struct wapi_list_s *list)
329: {
330:   FAR struct wapi_scan_info_s *info;
331: 
332:   /* Get current "wapi_info_t". */
333: 
334:   info = list->head.scan;
335: 
336:   /* Decode the event. */
337: 
338:   switch (event->cmd)
339:     {
340:     case SIOCGIWAP:
341:       {
342:         struct wapi_scan_info_s *temp;
343: 
344:         /* Allocate a new cell. */
345: 
346:         temp = malloc(sizeof(struct wapi_scan_info_s));
347:         if (!temp)
348:           {
349:             WAPI_STRERROR("malloc()");
350:             return -ENOMEM;
351:           }
352: 
353:         /* Reset it. */
354: 
355:         bzero(temp, sizeof(struct wapi_scan_info_s));
356:         temp->encode = 0xffff;
357: 
358:         /* Save cell identifier. */
359: 
360:         memcpy(&temp->ap, &event->u.ap_addr.sa_data,
361:                sizeof(struct ether_addr));
362: 
363:         /* Push it to the head of the list. */
364: 
365:         temp->next = info;
366:         list->head.scan = temp;
367: 
368:         break;
369:       }
370: 
371:     case SIOCGIWFREQ:
372:       {
373:         info->has_freq = 1;
374: 
375:         if (event->u.freq.e == 0)
376:           {
377:             /* Some drivers do not report frequency, but a channel.
378:              * Try to map this to frequency by assuming they are using
379:              * IEEE 802.11b/g.  But don't overwrite a previously parsed
380:              * frequency if the driver sends both frequency and channel,
381:              * since the driver may be sending an A-band channel that we
382:              * don't handle here.
383:              */
384: 
385:             if (event->u.freq.m >= 1 && event->u.freq.m <= 13)
386:               {
387:                 info->freq = 2407 + 5 * event->u.freq.m;
388:               }
389:             else if (event->u.freq.m == 14)
390:               {
391:                 info->freq = 2484;
392:               }
393:             else if (event->u.freq.m >= 36 && event->u.freq.m <= 165)
394:               {
395:                 info->freq = 5000 + 5 * event->u.freq.m;
396:               }
397:           }
398:         else
399:           {
400:             info->freq = wapi_freq2float(&(event->u.freq));
401:           }
402: 
403:         break;
404:       }
405: 
406:     case SIOCGIWMODE:
407:       {
408:         int ret = wapi_parse_mode(event->u.mode, &info->mode);
409:         if (ret >= 0)
410:           {
411:             info->has_mode = 1;
412:             break;
413:           }
414:         else
415:           {
416:             return ret;
417:           }
418:       }
419: 
420:     case SIOCGIWESSID:
421:       {
422:         info->has_essid = 1;
423:         info->essid_flag = (event->u.data.flags) ? WAPI_ESSID_ON
424:                                                  : WAPI_ESSID_OFF;
425:         memset(info->essid, 0, (WAPI_ESSID_MAX_SIZE + 1));
426:         if ((event->u.essid.pointer) && (event->u.essid.length))
427:           {
428:             memcpy(info->essid, event->u.essid.pointer,
429:                    event->u.essid.length);
430:           }
431: 
432:         break;
433:       }
434: 
435:     case SIOCGIWRATE:
436: 
437:       /* Scan may return a list of bitrates. As we have space for only a
438:        * single bitrate, we only keep the largest one.
439:        */
440: 
441:       if (!info->has_bitrate || event->u.bitrate.value > info->bitrate)
442:         {
443:           info->has_bitrate = 1;
444:           info->bitrate = event->u.bitrate.value;
445:         }
446: 
447:       break;
448: 
449:     case IWEVQUAL:
450:       {
451:         if (event->u.qual.updated & IW_QUAL_DBM)
452:           {
453:             info->has_rssi = 1;
454:             info->rssi = event->u.qual.level;
455: 
456:             /* Report signal levels in dBm */
457: 
458:             if (info->rssi >= 0x40)
459:               {
460:                 info->rssi -= 0x100;
461:               }
462:           }
463: 
464:         break;
465:       }
466: 
467:     case SIOCGIWENCODE:
468:       {
469:         info->has_encode = 1;
470:         info->encode = event->u.data.flags;
471:         break;
472:       }
473:     }
474: 
475:   return 0;
476: }

591:  ****************************************************************************/

593: int wapi_freq2chan(int sock, FAR const char *ifname, double freq,
594:                    FAR int *chan)
595: {
596:   struct iwreq wrq =
597:   {
598:   };
599: 
600:   char buf[sizeof(struct iw_range) * 2];
601:   int ret;
602: 
603:   WAPI_VALIDATE_PTR(chan);
604: 
605:   /* Prepare request. */
606: 
607:   bzero(buf, sizeof(buf));
608:   wrq.u.data.pointer = buf;
609:   wrq.u.data.length = sizeof(buf);
610:   wrq.u.data.flags = 0;

613:

632:         }
633: 
634:       /* Oops! Nothing found. */
635: 
636:       ret = -2;
637:     }
638:   else
639:     {
640:       int errcode = errno;
641:       WAPI_IOCTL_STRERROR(SIOCGIWRANGE, errcode);

643:     }

74: /****************************************************************************
75:  * Name: wpa_driver_wext_get_key_ext
76:  *
77:  * Description:
78:  *
79:  * Input Parameters:
80:  *   sockfd - Opened network socket
81:  *   ifname - Interface name
82:  *
83:  * Returned Value:
84:  *
85:  ****************************************************************************/
86: 
87: int wpa_driver_wext_get_key_ext(int sockfd, FAR const char *ifname,
88:                                 enum wpa_alg_e *alg, FAR char *key,
89:                                 size_t *req_len)
90: {
91:   struct iw_encode_ext *ext;
92:   struct iwreq iwr;
93:   int ret;
94: 
95:   ext = malloc(sizeof(*ext) + *req_len);
96:   if (ext == NULL)
97:     {
98:       return -ENOMEM;
99:     }
100: 
101:   memset(&iwr, 0, sizeof(iwr));
102:   strlcpy(iwr.ifr_name, ifname, IFNAMSIZ);
103: 
104:   iwr.u.encoding.pointer = (caddr_t) ext;
105:   iwr.u.encoding.length = sizeof(*ext) + *req_len;
106: 
107:   ret = ioctl(sockfd, SIOCGIWENCODEEXT, (unsigned long)&iwr);
108:   if (ret >= 0)
109:     {
110:       switch (ext->alg)
111:         {
112:           case IW_ENCODE_ALG_NONE:
113:             *alg = WPA_ALG_NONE;
114:             break;
115: 
116:           case IW_ENCODE_ALG_WEP:
117:             *alg = WPA_ALG_WEP;
118:             break;
119: 
120:           case IW_ENCODE_ALG_TKIP:
121:             *alg = WPA_ALG_TKIP;
122:             break;
123: 
124:           case IW_ENCODE_ALG_CCMP:
125:             *alg = WPA_ALG_CCMP;
126:             break;
127: 
128:           default:
129:             free(ext);
130:             return -EINVAL;
131:         }
132: 
133:      if (key && ext->key_len < *req_len)
134:        {
135:          memcpy(key, ext->key, ext->key_len);
136:          *req_len = ext->key_len;
137:        }
138:   }
139: 
140:   free(ext);
141:   return ret;
142: }

144: /****************************************************************************
145:  * Name: wpa_driver_wext_set_key_ext
146:  *
147:  * Description:
148:  *
149:  * Input Parameters:
150:  *   sockfd - Opened network socket
151:  *   ifname - Interface name
152:  *
153:  * Returned Value:
154:  *
155:  ****************************************************************************/
156: 
157: int wpa_driver_wext_set_key_ext(int sockfd, FAR const char *ifname,
158:                                 enum wpa_alg_e alg, FAR const char *key,
159:                                 size_t key_len)
160: {
161:   struct iwreq iwr;
162:   int ret = 0;
163:   struct iw_encode_ext *ext;
164: 
165:   DEBUGASSERT(ifname != NULL && key != NULL && key_len > 0);
166: 
167:   ext = malloc(sizeof(*ext) + key_len);
168:   if (ext == NULL)
169:     {
170:       return -ENOMEM;
171:     }
172: 
173:   memset(&iwr, 0, sizeof(iwr));
174:   strlcpy(iwr.ifr_name, ifname, IFNAMSIZ);
175: 
176:   iwr.u.encoding.pointer = (caddr_t) ext;
177:   iwr.u.encoding.length = sizeof(*ext) + key_len;
178: 
179:   if (key && key_len)
180:     {
181:       memcpy(ext + 1, key, key_len);
182:       ext->key_len = key_len;
183:     }
184: 
185:   switch (alg)
186:     {
187:       case WPA_ALG_NONE:
188:         ext->alg = IW_ENCODE_ALG_NONE;
189:         break;
190: 
191:       case WPA_ALG_WEP:
192:         ext->alg = IW_ENCODE_ALG_WEP;
193:         break;
194: 
195:       case WPA_ALG_TKIP:
196:         ext->alg = IW_ENCODE_ALG_TKIP;
197:         break;
198: 
199:       case WPA_ALG_CCMP:
200:         ext->alg = IW_ENCODE_ALG_CCMP;
201:         break;
202: 
203:       default:
204:         nerr("ERROR: Unknown algorithm %d", alg);
205:         free(ext);
206:         return -EINVAL;
207:     }
208: 
209:   if (ioctl(sockfd, SIOCSIWENCODEEXT, (unsigned long)&iwr) < 0)
210:     {
211:       ret = -errno;
212:       nerr("ERROR: ioctl[SIOCSIWENCODEEXT]: %d", errno);
213:     }
214: 
215:   free(ext);
216:   return ret;
217: }

219: /****************************************************************************
220:  * Name: wpa_driver_wext_associate
221:  *
222:  * Description:
223:  *
224:  * Input Parameters:
225:  *   wconfig - Describes the wireless configuration.
226:  *
227:  * Returned Value:
228:  *
229:  ****************************************************************************/

231: int wpa_driver_wext_associate(FAR struct wpa_wconfig_s *wconfig)
232: {
233:   struct iwreq req;
234:   int sockfd;
235:   int ret;
236: 
237:   DEBUGASSERT(wconfig != NULL);
238: 
239:   ninfo("sta_mode=%u auth_wpa=%08x cipher_mode=%08x alg=%d\n",
240:         wconfig->sta_mode, wconfig->auth_wpa, wconfig->cipher_mode,
241:         wconfig->alg);
242:   ninfo("ifname=%s ssid[%u]=%s passphrase[%u]=%s\n",
243:         wconfig->ifname, wconfig->ssidlen, wconfig->ssid, wconfig->phraselen,
244:         wconfig->passphrase);
245: 
246:   /* Get a socket (only so that we get access to the INET subsystem) */
247: 
248:   sockfd = wapi_make_socket();
249:   if (sockfd < 0)
250:     {
251:       return sockfd;
252:     }
253: 
254:   /* Put the driver name into the request */
255: 
256:   strlcpy(req.ifr_name, wconfig->ifname, IFNAMSIZ);
257: 
258:   ret = wapi_set_mode(sockfd, wconfig->ifname, wconfig->sta_mode);
259:   if (ret < 0)
260:     {
261:       nerr("ERROR: Fail set sta mode: %d\n", ret);
262:       goto close_socket;
263:     }
264: 
265:   ret = wpa_driver_wext_set_auth_param(sockfd, wconfig->ifname,
266:                                        IW_AUTH_WPA_VERSION,
267:                                        wconfig->auth_wpa);
268:   if (ret < 0)
269:     {
270:       nerr("ERROR: Fail set wpa version: %d\n", ret);
271:       goto close_socket;
272:     }
273: 
274:   ret = wpa_driver_wext_set_auth_param(sockfd, wconfig->ifname,
275:                                        IW_AUTH_CIPHER_PAIRWISE,
276:                                        wconfig->cipher_mode);
277:   if (ret < 0)
278:     {
279:       nerr("ERROR: Fail set cipher mode: %d\n", ret);
280:       goto close_socket;
281:     }
282: 
283:   if (wconfig->freq)
284:     {
285:       ret = wapi_set_freq(sockfd, wconfig->ifname,
286:                           wconfig->freq,
287:                           wconfig->flag == WAPI_FREQ_FIXED ?
288:                           IW_FREQ_FIXED : IW_FREQ_AUTO);
289:       if (ret < 0)
290:         {
291:           nerr("WARNING: Fail set freq: %d\n", ret);
292:         }
293:     }
294: 
295:   if (wconfig->phraselen > 0)
296:     {
297:       ret = wpa_driver_wext_set_key_ext(sockfd, wconfig->ifname,
298:                                         wconfig->alg,
299:                                         wconfig->passphrase,
300:                                         wconfig->phraselen);
301:       if (ret < 0)
302:         {
303:           nerr("ERROR: Fail set key: %d\n", ret);
304:           goto close_socket;
305:         }
306:     }
307: 
308:   if (wconfig->ssid)
309:     {
310:       ret = wapi_set_essid(sockfd, wconfig->ifname,
311:                            wconfig->ssid, WAPI_ESSID_ON);
312:       if (ret < 0)
313:         {
314:           nerr("ERROR: Fail set ssid: %d\n", ret);
315:           goto close_socket;
316:         }
317:     }
318:   else if (wconfig->bssid)
319:     {
320:       ret = wapi_set_ap(sockfd, wconfig->ifname,
321:                         (FAR const struct ether_addr *)wconfig->bssid);
322:       if (ret < 0)
323:         {
324:           nerr("ERROR: Fail set bssid: %d\n", ret);
325:         }
326:     }
327: 
328: close_socket:
329:   close(sockfd);
330:   return ret;
331: }

333: /****************************************************************************

336:  * Description:
337:  *
338:  * Input Parameters:
339:  *

341:  *
342:  ****************************************************************************/
343: 
344: static int wpa_driver_wext_process_auth_param(int sockfd,
345:                                               FAR const char *ifname,
346:                                               int idx,
347:                                               uint32_t *value,
348:                                               bool set)
349: {
350:   struct iwreq iwr;
351:   int errcode;
352:   int ret = 0;
353: 
354:   DEBUGASSERT(ifname != NULL);
355: 
356:   memset(&iwr, 0, sizeof(iwr));
357:   strlcpy(iwr.ifr_name, ifname, IFNAMSIZ);
358:   iwr.u.param.flags = idx & IW_AUTH_INDEX;
359:   iwr.u.param.value = set ? *value : 0;
360: 
361:   if (ioctl(sockfd, set ? SIOCSIWAUTH : SIOCGIWAUTH,
362:             (unsigned long)&iwr) < 0)
363:     {
364:       errcode = errno;
365:       if (errcode != EOPNOTSUPP)
366:         {
367:           nerr("ERROR: SIOCSIWAUTH(param %d value 0x%" PRIx32
368:                ") failed: %d)",
369:                idx, *value, errcode);
370:         }
371: 
372:       ret = -errcode;
373:     }
374: 
375:   if (ret == 0 && !set)
376:     {
377:       *value = iwr.u.param.value;
378:     }
379: 
380:   return ret;
381: }

419: /****************************************************************************
420:  * Name: wpa_driver_wext_disconnect
421:  *
422:  * Description:
423:  *
424:  * Input Parameters:
425:  *
426:  * Returned Value:
427:  *
428:  ****************************************************************************/
429: 
430: void wpa_driver_wext_disconnect(int sockfd, FAR const char *ifname)
431: {
432:   uint8_t ssid[WAPI_ESSID_MAX_SIZE + 1];
433:   const struct ether_addr bssid =
434:   {
435:   };
436: 
437:   struct iwreq iwr;
438:   int i;
439: 
440:   /* Only force-disconnect when the card is in infrastructure mode,
441:    * otherwise the driver might interpret the cleared BSSID and random
442:    * SSID as an attempt to create a new ad-hoc network.
443:    */
444: 
445:   memset(&iwr, 0, sizeof(iwr));
446:   strlcpy(iwr.ifr_name, ifname, IFNAMSIZ);
447: 
448:   if (ioctl(sockfd, SIOCGIWMODE, (unsigned long)&iwr) < 0)
449:     {
450:       nerr("ioctl[SIOCGIWMODE]: %s\n", strerror(errno));
451:       iwr.u.mode = IW_MODE_INFRA;
452:     }
453: 
454:   if (iwr.u.mode == IW_MODE_INFRA)
455:     {
456:       /* Clear the BSSID selection */
457: 
458:       if (wapi_set_ap(sockfd, ifname, &bssid) < 0)
459:         {
460:           nerr("WEXT: Failed to clear BSSID " "selection on disconnect\n");
461:         }
462: 
463:       /* Set a random SSID to make sure the driver will not be trying
464:        * to associate with something even if it does not understand
465:        * SIOCSIWMLME commands (or tries to associate automatically
466:        * after deauth/disassoc).
467:        */
468: 
469:       for (i = 0; i < WAPI_ESSID_MAX_SIZE; i++)
470:         {
471:           ssid[i] = rand() & 0xff;
472:         }
473: 
474:       ssid[WAPI_ESSID_MAX_SIZE] = '\0';
475: 
476:       if (wapi_set_essid(sockfd, ifname,
477:                          (FAR const char *)ssid, WAPI_ESSID_OFF) < 0)
478:         {
479:           nerr("WEXT: Failed to set bogus " "SSID to disconnect\n");
480:         }
481:     }

text: The binary RX bridge has another important ABI quirk: `bk_wifi_get_rx_buffer()` in the archive only consumes the first argument, stores the current pbuf globally, and `bk_wifi_clear_rx_buffer()` ignores its argument and frees that global pbuf. The source’s `header` out-parameter is therefore not actually populated; current behavior works only because the clear function ignores the uninitialized value. I’ll flag this as a vendor contract that should be wrapped/documented, not treated as a normal two-pointer API.

1393:                   wifi_mgmr_scan_adv(para, scan_complete_indicate,

1398:             }

1400:             {
